items.why: Shows a lightweight way to adapt trajectory selection to scene-dependent risk without retraining the world model.

items.title: PhysScope: Agentic Multimodal Physics Reasoning with Grounded Visual Memory
items.summary: Researchers introduce PhysScope, an inference-time visual harness that helps vision-language models self-correct physics scope mismatches without updating weights.
items.why: A weight-free harness for fixing premise errors in VLM reasoning is a practical technique for improving multimodal model reliability.

items.title: PeriaTrace: Tooth-Level Grounding Diagnosis and Patient-Facing Explanations from Periapical Radiographs
items.summary: Researchers introduced PeriaTrace, a three-stage framework that diagnoses teeth from periapical X-rays, generates visually grounded reports, and writes patient-friendly explanations.
items.why: Shows how grounding model findings to specific teeth and image regions can make medical imaging AI outputs more verifiable for clinicians.

items.title: ForecastGym: A Live, Controlled, and Replayable Benchmark for Forecasting Agents
items.summary: ForecastGym is a benchmark for LLM forecasting agents that controls retrieved web evidence and supports replayable evaluations.
items.why: Separating retrieval from reasoning gives teams a reproducible way to compare forecasting agents, models, and search strategies.

items.title: FrameRouter: Frame Budget Routing for Long-Video Understanding on Video-MME-v2 and Beyond
items.summary: FrameRouter proposes routing a fixed average frame budget across questions so each long-video query gets a different number of frames.
items.why: Adaptive frame allocation may improve long-video QA accuracy without increasing total compute, relevant to video pipeline design.

items.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Heat Pump and Underfloor Heating Control: An End-to-End Case Study
items.summary: A case study reports developing and deploying deep reinforcement learning to control underfloor heating with heat pumps in occupied buildings.
items.why: Documents a real-world deployment of DRL controllers, including the challenges of thermal inertia and comfort constraints.

items.title: Values Shape What Self-Improving Coding Agents Build
items.summary: A study finds that a short value statement in a self-improving coding agent's instruction file changes both its performance and the kind of software it builds.
items.why: Suggests agent instruction files can steer not just how well coding agents work but what they produce, a factor for agent configuration.

items.title: The Resolution Hypothesis: Agent Evolution's Key Is Identifying Improvements
items.summary: The paper argues agent evolution stalls mainly because noisy evaluations cannot reliably identify improved prompts, skills, or memories, not because proposals are poor.
items.why: Points to evaluation reliability as the bottleneck for self-improving agent loops, guiding where teams should invest.

items.title: Colombo: A Frontier-to-Frontier Autoresearch System for Oracle-Based Optimization
items.summary: Colombo is a self-organizing AI researcher system for oracle-based optimization that builds a living Complexity Atlas of achievable guarantees and unavoidable limits.

items.title: Hidden-State Similarity Predicts Re-Elicitation After Inoculation Prompting
items.summary: Research finds that hidden-state similarity, not just textual similarity, better predicts when inoculation prompts let harmful behavior re-emerge after fine-tuning.
items.why: Suggests text-based checks on inoculation prompts miss triggers, so safety evaluations should probe internal representations.

items.title: RSI-Prime: Training Models to Train Models
items.summary: RSI-Prime is a dataset of 350 experimental trajectories across seven task categories, aimed at teaching LLMs to conduct model training.
items.why: Targets LLMs making training decisions, a building block for recursive self-improvement pipelines that engineers should track.

items.title: WoRD: Diffusion-Based Posterior Inference for Online Goal Recognition
items.summary: WoRD uses diffusion-based posterior inference to recognize an agent's goal online from continuous trajectory prefixes without an explicit dynamics model.

items.title: Agent Trust Infrastructure (ATI): A Federated Identity, Trust, Attestation, and Accountability Architecture for Cross-Organization Autonomous AI Agents
items.summary: Agent Trust Infrastructure proposes a framework-independent security architecture using PKI, Zero Trust, and remote attestation for verifying cross-organization AI agent identity and authorization.
items.why: Addresses a practical gap for enterprises letting agents from independent organizations invoke tools and act across boundaries.

items.title: Analyzing Learned Convnet Features with Dirichlet Process Gaussian Mixture Models
items.summary: A 2017 arXiv paper proposes clustering internal convnet representations with a Dirichlet Process Gaussian Mixture Model to help visualize and interpret learned features.

items.title: Improved Convergence Rates for Stochastic Multi-Gradient Descent which Close the Gap: A Proof by AI
items.summary: A note claims an improved convergence rate for stochastic multi-gradient descent, giving a squared Pareto-stationarity rate of about T^-1 under standard assumptions.

items.title: Continual-ARC: Measuring Skill Acquisition over a Working Lifetime
items.summary: Continual-ARC is a lifelong benchmark built from ARC-AGI editions that tests skill acquisition over time, comparing memory-based and weight-based learners on the same stream.
items.why: Offers a common benchmark for comparing memory-based and weight-based continual learning systems, useful for evaluating agent designs.

items.title: Fragmented Markers, Mixed Results: A Systematic Review of AI Coding Assistants and Developer Productivity
items.summary: A staged systematic review aims to synthesize studies of AI coding assistants' effects on developer productivity, addressing inconsistent productivity measures across studies.
items.why: Highlights that productivity claims for coding assistants rest on incomparable metrics, which matters when justifying tool adoption.

items.title: Measuring Human-AI Alignment as an Early Indicator for Effective Collaboration in Hybrid SE Teams
items.summary: A position paper proposes a research agenda for a static, SE-specific metric suite to measure early alignment between AI agents and human expectations in software teams.
items.why: Offers a way to assess human-AI alignment before runtime, which may help teams plan collaboration with AI agents in software work.

items.title: Can AI Help Explain AI? Effects of Multimodal LLM-Generated Explanations on Perceived Understanding and Perceived Trust in XAI Visualizations
items.summary: A pre-registered study with 128 participants found that LLM-generated textual explanations improved perceived understanding and trust in XAI visualizations.
items.why: Suggests pairing XAI visuals with LLM-written text can make model explanations easier for end users to interpret and trust.

items.title: RAW: Refusal Aversion in the Wild, A Causal Measurement Method for Deployed LLMs
items.summary: The paper introduces RAW, a method using LLM stochasticity as a natural experiment to causally measure how refusals affect user disengagement on deployed models.
items.why: Gives platform teams a way to measure the user-side cost of refusals without A/B testing refusal behavior, which is often constrained.

items.title: Can an LLM dream? Testing the overfitted brain hypothesis on an agent with text memory
items.summary: Researchers test the overfitted brain hypothesis by having an LLM agent rewrite a text memory nightly from conversation transcripts that are partly corrupted.
items.why: Explores how memory-update routines in LLM agents respond to noisy input, a design concern for agents that persist their own memory.

items.title: Literary Language Mashup: Curating Fictions with Large Language Models
items.summary: The paper uses LLMs as evaluators of Spanish and English microfiction and short stories, comparing their judgments with those of human literary judges.

items.title: From Preference Data to Personalization: Tracing Sycophancy in Large Language Models
items.summary: The paper defines sycophancy as inappropriate agreement and introduces a validity-aware grader and SycoDrift, a 3,298-probe evaluation set.
items.why: Provides a more precise benchmark for separating appropriate agreement from sycophancy, useful when evaluating assistant behavior.

items.title: Consistency Is Not Correction: Separating Confidence, Abstention, and Recovery in LLM Agents
items.summary: The paper decomposes confidence-based controller benefits into discrimination, selective prediction, and correction utility, showing these claims do not follow from one another.
items.why: Warns teams that a confidence signal ranking answers does not guarantee it improves answers when used to resample, escalate, or abstain.

items.title: Evaluating Semantic Insensitivity in Financial Sentiment Analysis: Implications for Sustainable Financial Decision-Making
items.summary: The paper presents Agent-driven Semantic Inversion, an LLM multi-agent attack that manipulates financial text to fool FinBERT-style sentiment models.
items.why: Shows that high-accuracy financial sentiment models can be fooled by subtle adversarial text edits, a risk for automated trading pipelines.

items.title: Depth-Aware Activation Steering via Attention Residuals
items.summary: The paper combines Attention Residuals and Jacobian-lens readout into a depth-aware activation steering pipeline, tested on two small Qwen3 open models.
items.why: Offers a training-free way to distribute steering vectors across layers, though results are shown only on small open models.

items.title: Token Commitment as a Control Surface for Steering Masked Diffusion Generation
items.summary: The paper treats token commitment in masked diffusion models as a steering control surface, separating which tokens to commit and how many to commit per step.
items.why: Highlights decoding-policy choices as a lever for steering diffusion language models without modifying activations or logits.

items.title: FCP: Formal Context Protocol for Verifying LLM-Generated Artifacts
items.summary: The Formal Context Protocol (FCP) checks AI-generated artifacts against the request, separating formal conformance verified by solvers from prose fidelity.
items.why: Addresses the weakness of model-written tests that validate model-written artifacts, offering a path to stronger verification of generated code.

items.title: EgoLink: Egocentric Language-Vision Interactive Network Knowledge Challenge Summary
items.summary: The EgoLink Challenge summary describes benchmarks for egocentric multimodal social reasoning and interactive agents that complete service tasks via tool use.

items.title: AdaFlowLite: Scalable and Non-blocking Inference on Asynchronous Mobile Data
items.summary: AdaFlowLite proposes non-blocking inference over asynchronous multi-sensor mobile data, balancing waiting for slow inputs against accuracy loss.
items.why: Relevant to engineers building distributed sensing systems where sensor data arrives at variable times.

items.title: TIBECG: Temporal Information Bottleneck for Lead-Specific Demographic Privacy in ECG Waveform Release
items.summary: TIBECG applies a temporal information bottleneck to ECG waveforms to limit demographic information leakage while retaining diagnostic content across 6,386 recordings.
items.why: Shows a method for reducing demographic privacy leakage in shared medical signal data while keeping most clinical utility.

items.title: Stop Early, Stay Simple: Evidence Acquisition for Power System Fault and Attack Diagnosis
items.summary: ActiGrid is a benchmark for active evidence acquisition in power system fault diagnosis, where a DQN decides whether to request another telemetry source or stop.
items.why: Tests whether learned policies for selecting diagnostic evidence justify their added complexity in cyber-physical grid monitoring.

items.title: Watermark Evidence under Open-Weight LLM Modification: Exact Bounds for Low-Rank Output Watermarks
items.summary: Researchers derive exact bounds on how modifying open-weight LLMs affects the evidence available to OpenStamp-style output watermark verifiers.
items.why: Shows how weight modifications can weaken watermark detection, relevant to anyone relying on output watermarks for provenance of open-weight models.

items.title: Disambiguating Moral Circuits and Moral Features in Language Models: Moral content, normative judgment or cue words? Evidence from 14 models
items.summary: Researchers test whether interpretability-identified attention heads and SAE features respond to moral content, normative judgment, or just the cue word 'morally' across 14 models.

items.title: Bookkeeping Is Not Judgement: EJBench, an Engineering Judgement Benchmark Built from a Conjugate Heat Transfer Design Campaign
items.summary: Researchers introduce EJBench, a benchmark testing whether models can predict engineering design behavior at new conditions without running simulations, built from battery cold plate heat transfer work.
items.why: Suggests current agent benchmarks measure software operation rather than engineering judgment, a gap to consider when evaluating AI for technical decisions.

items.title: From Top to Bottom: Quark Mass Hierarchies in Heterotic String Theory
items.summary: A paper studies whether quark mass hierarchies can arise perturbatively at tree level in smooth heterotic Calabi-Yau string compactifications.

items.title: Margin Dynamics for Large Language Model Alignment
items.summary: Researchers provide a theoretical framework modeling LLM alignment methods as vector fields, deriving closed-form margin dynamics for DPO and IPO.
items.why: Offers theory explaining why DPO margins grow without bound while IPO margins converge, informing choice among alignment methods.

items.title: LLMs as Validators for Cross-Chain Bridges: Evaluating Source-Level and Transaction-Level Attack Detection on Solana
items.summary: Researchers evaluate whether LLMs can detect source-level and transaction-level attacks in a native Rust Solana lock-and-mint bridge with four exploitable variants.
items.why: Tests whether LLMs can diagnose cross-chain bridge vulnerabilities from code or transactions, relevant to teams auditing on-chain programs.

items.title: Beyond Reconstruction: A Unified Framework for Trustworthy and Explainable EEG Artifact Removal Evaluation
items.summary: Researchers propose TriX-EEG, a three-level framework that evaluates EEG artifact removal models beyond reconstruction metrics, checking signal validity and explainability.

items.title: Revisiting the Survival of Agent-Attributed Code: How Measurement Choices Decide the Verdict
items.summary: A study re-examines survival of AI agent-written code across 854,139 lines in 215 repositories, varying nine measurement choices to see how they change the verdict.
items.why: Shows conflicting findings about agent code retention depend heavily on measurement choices, which matters when judging agent code quality metrics.

items.title: Can Coding Agents Write and Transpile Unit Tests
items.summary: Researchers benchmark three popular coding agents on writing unit tests and transpiling them between programming languages using frontier models.
items.why: Tests whether agent-written tests can be trusted to validate agent-generated code, a concern for teams relying on agents for code modernization.

items.title: SimAI: Mechanistic User Simulation through Psychological Network Models
items.summary: SimAI, a framework for mechanistic user simulation, models psychological factors shaping user responses and uses graph reconstruction rewards to supervise simulated conversations.

items.title: Evaluating the Evaluation of Music Generation Models with Generative Psychometrics
items.summary: Researchers map subjective evaluation methods in ISMIR music generation papers from 2020-2025 and apply generative psychometrics to assess item stability.

items.title: ARC-2: Continuous Compliance Through Delta Management
items.summary: ARC-2 proposes Delta Management, a continuous governance framework that measures deviations of autonomous systems from their certified baseline after deployment.
items.why: Addresses post-deployment compliance for autonomous systems, a governance gap for teams operating certified AI in production.

items.title: TUSI: A Citation-Grounded Graph-Based Benchmark
items.summary: Researchers introduce TUSI-Bench, a citation-grounded Persian legal benchmark for evaluating retrieval-augmented generation systems.

items.title: Coordination of Heterogeneous Teams with Uncertain Task Requirements
items.summary: Researchers present a hierarchical planner using a graph neural network and shortest-path search to coordinate heterogeneous agent teams facing uncertain task requirements.

items.title: EmbedGym: Letting Coding Agents Develop and Debug Embedded Firmware Without Physical Hardware
items.summary: EmbedGym is presented as an environment letting coding agents develop and debug embedded firmware without physical hardware, addressing the lack of hardware feedback in agent loops.
items.why: Gives agents a closed feedback loop for firmware bugs like timing and bus protocol issues that compile-only testing misses.

items.title: Inventa: Decentralized Self-Improving Agents for Autonomous Scientific Discovery
items.summary: Inventa is a framework for automated scientific discovery that uses autonomous, decentralized self-improving LLM research agents to generate more diverse and feasible ideas.
items.why: It targets agent failure modes like convergence on similar ideas and propagation of unsupported claims through shared memory, relevant to multi-agent system design.

items.title: AR-WAM: efficient streaming world-action modeling for autonomous driving
items.summary: AR-WAM is a streaming world-action model for autonomous driving that combines autoregressive temporal modeling with single-pass future conditioning to reduce the cost of video-based prediction.
items.why: It addresses the compute cost of repeated history encoding and iterative video generation, which limits using video foundation models in real-time driving.

items.title: The Hidden Cost of MoE Diffusion Decoding: Profiling and Fixing the Sampler
items.summary: Profiling of a 26B diffusion Mixture-of-Experts language model on an edge accelerator found the per-token logits sampling pipeline, not expert GEMMs, is the largest decode-time cost after quantization.
items.why: Engineers optimizing diffusion LLM inference should look beyond matrix multiplications, since the sampler can dominate decode time on bandwidth-bound hardware.

items.title: PromptPack: Training-Free Augmentation of Diffusion Editors for Intent-Aligned Spatial and Semantic Control
items.summary: PromptPack is a training-free method that adds Keep, Permit, and Modify edit guides to diffusion image editors for spatial and semantic control over changes.
items.why: It offers a way to add precise region-level control to existing diffusion editors without retraining.

items.title: FaceRiff: Data-Efficient Unified Text-to-3D Face Asset Synthesis via Geometric Conditioning
items.summary: FaceRiff is a framework for synthesizing text-to-3D face assets with UV-aligned geometry, albedo, and displacement, using geometric conditioning on image diffusion models.
items.why: It aims to reduce dependence on scarce specialized facial datasets for digital-human rendering pipelines.

items.title: Cancellation-Free Constrained SquareCB for Safe Controller Selection
items.summary: The paper proposes a cancellation-free constrained SquareCB contextual bandit that uses a rectified cost weight, so slack in some rounds cannot offset budget violations in others.
items.why: It gives a theoretical approach to safe controller selection where cost budgets must hold, relevant to safety-constrained decision systems.

items.title: Domain-Tuned Diffusion Super-Resolution for 4K Facial Asset Maps
items.summary: Researchers present a domain-tuned diffusion upscaler that takes facial albedo and displacement maps from 1K to 4K using an adapted frozen SDXL backbone.
items.why: It addresses 4K facial asset quality for cinematic rendering, where generic photo super-resolution fails on UV-map statistics and height-field errors.

items.title: A Temporal Algebraic Framework for Data Stream Evaluation Under Delayed Labels and Distribution Shifts
items.summary: The paper extends an algebraic framework for evaluating data streams with delayed labels and distribution shifts, using fading or sliding-window weighting with O(m^2) update cost per step.
items.why: It helps teams separate true model degradation from prevalence drift when evaluating streaming classifiers with late labels.

items.title: ALOHA Lightning: Learning Fast and Precise Manipulation
items.summary: ALOHA Lightning is a system that uses kinesthetic teaching to collect near-human-speed demonstrations for training fast and precise robotic manipulation policies.
items.why: It targets the gap between learned robot policy speed and human speed, a practical bottleneck for deploying manipulation learning.

items.title: V2V Communications Using Blockchain-Enabled 6G Technology and Federated Learning
items.summary: A study proposes vehicle-to-vehicle communication combining blockchain-enabled 6G, federated learning, and latency and resource allocation optimization, with k-anonymity for privacy.
items.why: The abstract gives few implementation details, so its practical relevance for engineering teams is limited.

items.title: Does the Model Use What It Cites? Counterfactual Tests of Grounded Reasoning Chains in Small Video-Language Models
items.summary: The paper tests whether small video-language models actually use the regions they cite by blacking out cited regions and measuring how often correct answers flip.
items.why: It offers an annotation-free intervention test for whether grounded reasoning citations reflect real model dependence.

items.title: Benchmarking Deep Learning Models for Wheelchair Configuration Classification in Accessible Automated Vehicle Applications
items.summary: Researchers benchmark deep learning models for classifying wheelchair configurations, aiming to support accessible automated vehicle design.

items.title: ThermLeT: Transformer-based Temperature Prediction for 2.5D Chiplet Architecture
items.summary: ThermLeT is a transformer-based surrogate that predicts steady-state temperature in 2.5D chiplet packages in 13 ms, about four orders of magnitude faster than ANSYS-style finite element solvers.
items.why: Fast thermal surrogates can speed design space exploration for dense heterogeneous chiplet packages.

items.title: Eight in Ten LLMs Leak System-Prompt Secrets: Nevan, an Agentic Capture-the-Flag Study
items.summary: An audit of 363 OpenRouter text models found an agentic AI attacker exfiltrated a secret system-prompt flag from 296 of them.
items.why: Engineers deploying LLMs with secrets in system prompts should assume they can be extracted, so secrets should not live there.

items.title: Weight-space programming for tractor guidance controller: large language models natively write neural network weights that steer a real tractor
items.summary: Researchers report LLMs editing a neural network's weights directly from natural language specs to adapt tractor steering control, tested on a real tractor.
items.why: It demonstrates LLM-driven weight editing controlling physical hardware, though the abstract provides limited detail on robustness.

items.title: OCCAM: Improved Single-Cell Representation Learning and Perturbation Effect Prediction
items.summary: Researchers introduce OCCAM, an MLP framework combining denoised cell representations with gene, text, and protein features to predict genetic perturbation effects.
items.why: It offers a method for predicting perturbation effects across unseen cell contexts and gene combinations, relevant to computational biology pipelines.

items.title: Pathology Randomization for Synthetic Priors and Zero-Shot Detection
items.summary: Researchers propose pathology randomization to build synthetic priors for zero-shot abnormality detection in hospital brain imaging across contrasts and resolutions.

items.title: Modeling Document and Section Hierarchies in Embedding Space
items.summary: Researchers propose the Hierarchical Embedded Topic Model, which represents documents as multiple sections with their own topic structure rather than a single topic distribution.

items.title: DiagTrace: An Interactive Benchmark for Clinical Decision Making
items.summary: Researchers released DiagTrace, a source-grounded benchmark testing whether LLMs can reconstruct documented diagnostic trajectories when patient information is revealed incrementally.
items.why: It shows how LLM evaluation can move beyond upfront-information medical QA toward interactive, evidence-gathering diagnosis tests.

items.title: Computed Permutation Trellis Coding: Near-Optimal Quantization from Two Multiplications and a 64-Byte Table
items.summary: Researchers propose Computed Permutation Trellis Coding, a low-bit tensor quantization format whose decoder needs only two multiplications and a 64-byte table.
items.why: It targets near-optimal low-bit quantization with a small decoder, relevant to model weight compression for inference.

items.title: GauntletScore: Auditable Fact-Checking That Matches the Best Published Checkers on LLM-AggreFact
items.summary: Researchers describe GauntletScore, an auditable fact-checking system that aggregates independent readers' answers and reports results matching the best published checkers on LLM-AggreFact.
items.why: It offers an auditable, evidence-ledger approach to verifying whether generated text is supported by its source.

items.title: RLDE: A Reinforcement Learning Framework for Interpretable Iterative Document Editing
items.summary: Researchers propose RLDE, a reinforcement learning framework that frames iterative document editing as a reference-free MDP to produce interpretable revisions.

items.title: FM-Mamba: An Efficient Native 2D Selective State Space Model with Stability-Aware Discretization
items.summary: Researchers propose FM-Mamba, a native 2D selective state space model built on the Fornasini–Marchesini model with stability-aware discretization for image features.

items.title: Segmentation-Guided Direct Capacity Estimation of Rooftop Photovoltaics from Aerial Imagery
items.summary: Researchers propose Direct Head, a segmentation-guided architecture that regresses rooftop PV capacity directly from aerial imagery instead of converting segmented area to power.
items.why: It is a niche application of computer vision to energy planning, with limited direct relevance to most engineering teams.

items.title: HyCoInfer: Cloud-Edge Collaborative Inference for Large Language Models on Heterogeneous GPU-FPGA Architectures
items.summary: Researchers present HyCoInfer, a cloud-edge serving system that runs LLM prefill on cloud GPUs and distributes decoding across cloud GPUs and edge FPGAs.
items.why: It suggests heterogeneous GPU-FPGA serving could improve decoding efficiency for LLM inference, a cost and infrastructure consideration.

items.title: When AUC Meets Generative Reconstruction: A Unified Principle for Balanced Visual Representation Learning
items.summary: Researchers propose a unified principle for balancing contrastive and generative objectives when training visual encoders for multimodal large language models.
items.why: It addresses a known trade-off in visual encoder training that affects multimodal LLM feature quality.

items.title: Semantic Communication via Analog RF Computing: When the Radio Computes the Meaning
items.summary: Researchers propose a semantic communication framework that runs the semantic encoder in an edge device's RF receiver front end using analog RF computing.

items.title: RoboTeam: Benchmarking Vision-Based Multi-Agent Control of Many Robot Arms in Real Time
items.summary: Researchers present RoboTeam, a simulated real-time benchmark where multimodal agents control 4 to 16 robot arms from camera images across 36 long cooperative tasks.
items.why: It provides a harder benchmark for multi-agent embodied control that avoids pausing the world and ground-truth object positions.

items.title: When does deep reinforcement learning pay off in HVAC supervisory control? Four small Modelica case studies trained directly on FMUs
items.summary: Researchers examine four small Modelica case studies of HVAC supervisory control to assess when deep reinforcement learning outperforms baselines, trained directly on FMUs.
items.why: It offers a rigorous check on when DRL gains are real versus weak baselines, useful for industrial control projects.

items.title: EgoHandWAM: Probing the Role of Hand Motion in Egocentric World Action Modeling
items.summary: Researchers present EgoHandWAM, which forecasts 3D wrist and fingertip trajectories and future visual features from egocentric images and hand states, trained on 751,065 windows.

items.title: What RL on Expert-Built Tasks Teaches Nemotron 3.5 Super
items.summary: Researchers post-trained NVIDIA's Nemotron 3.5 Super with reinforcement learning on five expert-built task datasets, training a separate LoRA adapter for each.
items.why: Shows how targeted RL on domain tasks can change a large open model's behavior, with per-task adapters compared against the base model.

items.title: CueClash: Frontier Vision-Language Models Judge 3-D Relations Close to the Picture Plane
items.summary: CueClash is a benchmark of rendered scenes that tests whether vision-language models judge 3-D relations from 2-D picture cues or from the actual ground layout.
items.why: Reveals that frontier VLMs rely heavily on 2-D picture shortcuts, a reliability concern for spatial reasoning in deployed vision systems.

items.title: From Imperfective Paradox to Moorean Absurdity: Single-Chain Reasoning Lock-In and Multi-Candidate Verbalization Across Aspectual and Pragmatic Ambiguity
items.summary: Researchers test a single-chain premature lock-in hypothesis in Qwen3-8B across four preregistered experiments on aspectual and pragmatic ambiguity in language judgments.

items.title: EGS: A Complementary Safety Framework for Educational LLMs
items.summary: The paper introduces the Educational Guardrail System, a lightweight, model-agnostic runtime framework for safer adolescent-facing LLM education tools.
items.why: Offers a runtime moderation layer that adds contextual guidance beyond binary refusals, relevant to teams deploying LLMs to students.

items.title: Communicate the Change: Efficient Expert Parallelism via Activation Compression
items.summary: The paper proposes compressing activations to reduce communication in expert parallelism for sparse mixture-of-experts LLM inference.
items.why: Targets the synchronous dispatch and combine communication bottleneck in MoE inference, a real cost at large scale.

items.title: Learning Optimal Transport Plans Via Autoregressive Token Regression
items.summary: ToR-OT is a transformer model that learns to predict optimal transport plans via autoregressive token regression, benchmarked against classical solvers.

items.title: Solver-Free and Cost-Aware Online Scheduling of AI Data Center Tasks
items.summary: The paper presents a solver-free online scheduling rule that assigns AI data center tasks start periods to reduce electricity cost, tested on an A100 GPU trace.
items.why: Offers a fast, cost-aware scheduling approach for AI clusters that avoids running a solver for every arriving task.

items.title: OAK-Mind: Zero-Training Mental Health Change Inference from Passive Sensing via Knowledge-Grounded Multi-Agent LLMs
items.summary: OAK-Mind is a multi-agent LLM framework that infers mental health change from passive wearable and smartphone sensing without task-specific training.

items.title: PCGRL for Complex Platformers: Synthesizing Playable and Diverse Levels via Inflated Envelopes and Forward Curricula
items.summary: The paper presents an improved PCGRL approach for generating playable, diverse platformer levels using inflated envelopes and forward curricula.

items.title: OfficePrism: Benchmarking Agents on Single-Domain Operations Across Enterprise Business Functions
items.summary: OfficePrism is a benchmark of 420 single-domain enterprise tasks across seven business functions for evaluating AI agents.
items.why: Isolates single-function competence from cross-function coordination, helping teams localize agent failures before deploying them in enterprise workflows.

items.title: Anticipating or Speculating? Making Futures Pay in AI Ethics
items.summary: The paper argues that uniform decision rules for physician disagreement with medical AI systems are flawed because appropriate use is context-specific and empirical.

items.title: Teaching Language Models to Narrow Boolean Patent Searches from Search Feedback
items.summary: The paper distills 38,397 Japan Patent Office search reports into strategies and trains a generator to write Boolean patent queries with higher precision.
items.why: Shows how search feedback can train LLMs to produce narrower, screenable Boolean queries for professional retrieval workflows.

items.title: Neural Network Path Optimization for Finding Transition States on a Machine Learned Potential
items.summary: The paper proposes a neural network path optimization method for finding chemical transition states on machine-learned interatomic potentials.
items.why: Uses MLIPs with automatic differentiation to make transition-state search cheaper than DFT-based path methods.

items.title: When the World Is the Test Suite: Agentic Intelligence for the Physical World
items.summary: The paper examines coding agents that write, test, and repair programs for robots, labs, and industrial controllers, where the physical world serves as the test suite.
items.why: Highlights that verifying agent-written control code requires costly physical or simulated runs, changing how evaluation must be designed.

items.title: Perception into Imagination: Executable Memory for World Models
items.summary: The paper introduces executable perceptual memory, a world-model framework that tracks explicit perceptual state alongside latent dynamics during imagination for physical agents.

items.title: FIRE-Drive: Feasibility-Informed Risk Evaluation for End-to-End Diffusion Planning
items.summary: FIRE-Drive proposes a feasibility-informed risk evaluation method for diffusion-based end-to-end autonomous driving planning, targeting infeasible trajectory proposals and mode selection.
items.why: It addresses infeasible proposals and safety-aware mode selection in diffusion planners, relevant to teams building autonomous driving stacks.

items.title: Agent Trajectories as Evidence for Software Quality Assurance
items.summary: The paper proposes analyzing observable AI agent trajectories, alongside specifications and generated artifacts, as evidence to target software quality assurance.
items.why: It suggests using agent action logs to find consequential decisions and hidden assumptions that passing tests may miss.

items.title: An AI-Driven Assistant for Human-Centric Building Digital Twin Systems: Design, Implementation, and Comparative User Evaluation
items.summary: Researchers present an AI-driven conversational assistant for a human-centric building digital twin system, monitoring indoor environmental quality, with a comparative user evaluation.

items.title: FailureGen: Scalable Robot Failure Data Generation with World Models
items.summary: FailureGen is a method that generates synthetic robot failure videos with temporal annotations by fine-tuning a Cosmos world model and reusing action trajectories from recorded failures.
items.why: Synthetic failure data could help robot learning teams cover failure scenarios that are costly to collect at scale.

items.title: Leveraging Segmentation Representations for Efficient Classification: A Self-Configuring Framework Based on nnU-Net
items.summary: A self-configuring framework extends nnU-Net to 3D medical image classification by reusing segmentation model representations in a lightweight classifier.
items.why: Reusing segmentation features for classification could cut the cost of building separate medical imaging classifiers.

items.title: RICoT: Recurrent Interleaved Chain-of-Thought for Page Stream Segmentation
items.summary: RICoT is a prompting framework that treats page stream segmentation as a sequential process over whole document streams using recurrent interleaved chain-of-thought with LLMs.
items.why: It offers a prompting approach for splitting multi-page documents, an alternative to boundary classification over neighboring pages.

items.title: Deal With It: On Better Schedules for Listwise Reranking
items.summary: The paper studies how to split candidates across parallel calls in listwise LLM reranking, finding round-robin splitting by retriever rank minimizes expected cuts when quotas bind.
items.why: Scheduling choices affect how many costly repair calls listwise rerankers need in retrieval pipelines.

items.title: Encoding, Decodability, and Use: A Five-Layer Framework for Benchmark Measurement Audits with Evidence from UAV Intent Recognition
items.summary: The authors propose a five-layer framework for auditing benchmark measurements, instantiated on UAV intent recognition, separating encoding, decodability, and use of model information.
items.why: It warns that benchmark accuracy may not show a model understands the target construct, which matters for evaluation design.

items.title: Eyes in the Update? Learning Where Rewards Land in Multimodal Reasoning
items.summary: Researchers study how to allocate trajectory-level rewards to specific tokens in multimodal reinforcement learning for image and video reasoning.
items.why: Better reward credit assignment could improve post-training of vision-language reasoning models.

items.title: As Student Rollouts Continue, Visual Backdoors Keep Growing
items.summary: The paper examines how visual backdoors can propagate from teacher to student vision-language models during on-policy distillation.
items.why: Post-training distillation pipelines for VLMs may carry backdoor risks from teacher models that teams need to test for.

items.title: MAVE: Reconstructing Editable 3D Blockouts from Film Shots
items.summary: MAVE is a video-to-blockout framework that reconstructs editable 3D animated blockouts from film shots, released alongside a 50-shot benchmark called MAVEBench.
items.why: Automated blockout reconstruction could lower the cost of previsualization and create paired training data for video generation.

items.title: LeViT-UNet++: Towards Balanced Fine-Grained Details and Context for Efficient Medical Image Segmentation
items.summary: LeViT-UNet++ is proposed as an efficient medical image segmentation model that balances fine-grained details and global context under limited compute.

items.title: Manufacturing Differential Sparsity: Planner-Hardware Co-Design for Efficient World Model Planning
items.summary: The paper proposes planner-hardware co-design that exploits latent locality in quantized JEPA-style world model predictors to speed up model predictive control planning for embodied agents.
items.why: Hardware-exploitable locality could make world-model planning for robots fast enough for real-time control.

items.title: Motion-Aware Reward Modeling for Instruction-Guided Video Editing
items.summary: The paper identifies motion collapse in reward models for instruction-guided video editing, where rewards favor temporal consistency over motion, and studies motion-aware reward modeling.
items.why: Reward models that ignore motion can be exploited during fine-tuning, which affects teams training video editing systems.

items.title: Right Labels, Wrong Reasons: Signed Feature Attribution for Multi-Label Explainability
items.summary: FLEX (Fisher LDA Explainer) is proposed as a global surrogate that gives signed feature attributions per label for multi-label classifiers.
items.why: Per-label signed attributions offer a way to check whether multi-label classifiers are right for the wrong reasons.

items.title: DGF-Asym: Adaptive Peer Weighting for Collective Estimation under Noisy and Faulty Sensing
items.summary: Researchers propose DGF-Asym, a decentralized method that lets robots weight peer information asymmetrically for collective estimation under noisy, faulty sensing.
items.why: It offers a way for robot swarms to reach consensus without prior sensor-noise statistics or explicit fault models, while communicating asynchronously.

items.title: Testing World Models on Actions They Have Never Seen: Held-Out Plans, Forecast Accuracy and Price Rules in Retail
items.summary: Researchers propose a test of whether action-conditioned world models can accurately predict outcomes for actions held out of training, using retail price and promotion plans across 2,853 models.
items.why: It suggests forecast accuracy alone may not reliably indicate whether a world model can answer what-if questions about unseen actions.

items.title: JET: Just-Enough Exploration Tuning for Efficient Tool-Calling Agents in Repository-Level Question Answering
items.summary: Researchers identify over-exploration in LLM agents that keep calling tools after gathering enough information, and propose JET, a tuning method to curb it in repository QA.
items.why: Excess tool calls raise latency and cost for coding agents, and standard supervised fine-tuning can propagate the behavior.

items.title: From Perception to Simulation: Unveiling and Empowering Mental Spatial Dynamics in MLLMs
items.summary: Researchers introduce MentalGrid, a benchmark testing whether multimodal LLMs can simulate evolving spatial states without intermediate visual feedback, finding significant deficiencies.
items.why: It highlights a gap in dynamic spatial reasoning that matters for embodied and robotics applications built on multimodal models.

items.title: JointGV: Structure-Aware Correction of Visual World Models with Parallel Graph Dynamics for Long-Horizon Modeling
items.summary: Researchers propose JointGV, a plug-in that uses a separately predicted relational graph state to correct drift in visual world models over long horizons.
items.why: Reducing recursive error in visual world models could improve long-horizon robot planning and control without restructuring the visual model.

items.title: Do LLMs Understand Network Traces? A Comparative Study of Reasoning over Raw and Filtered Traffic Data
items.summary: A study evaluates whether LLMs reliably extract packet-level fields and reconstruct flows from raw versus filtered network traffic data.
items.why: It tests whether LLMs can automate network traffic investigation, a task that currently requires substantial technical expertise.

items.title: Evolution Under Fire: Evolving Agent Safety Harnesses with Adaptive Injection Stressors
items.summary: Researchers introduce Evolution Under Fire, a framework that co-evolves agent safety harnesses and adaptive injection stressors to defend tool-using agents against malicious instructions.
items.why: Tool-using agents processing untrusted emails and webpages face prompt injection risk, and static hand-designed defenses require repeated manual redesign.

items.title: Adaptive LLM-Driven Honeypots vs. LLM-Driven Attackers: Does Narrative Coherence Improve Deception?
items.summary: A paper proposes narrative deception, where LLM-driven honeypots generate coherent artefacts mapped to MITRE ATT&CK techniques, and tests whether coherence retains attackers better.
items.why: As autonomous LLM-driven offensive agents emerge, coherent deceptive responses may be a practical defensive strategy for security teams.

items.title: Hierarchical Control of Antiphase Synchronization in Biomorphic Spiking Neural Architectures for Locomotor Control
items.summary: Researchers present a framework for identifying and stabilizing antiphase synchronization in a biomorphic spiking central pattern generator embedded in a neuromuscular loop.

items.title: AlignedHPO: Efficient Surrogate-Guided Loss Hyperparameter Optimization
items.summary: Researchers propose AlignedHPO, a framework that tunes differentiable loss hyperparameters using gradient alignment, Jacobian-vector products, and surrogate validation objectives.
items.why: It aims to replace expensive black-box tuning of loss hyperparameters with a cheaper gradient-based method in deep learning training.

items.title: FVScore: Specification-Driven Neuro-Symbolic Video Evaluation
items.summary: Researchers introduce FVScore, a neuro-symbolic framework that evaluates generated videos by compiling prompt and implicit constraints into propositions and tracing temporal violations.
items.why: It offers a more traceable alternative to holistic MLLM judges for evaluating video generation quality.

items.title: CULypso: A Clustered Federated Unlearning paradigm for Vehicular Ad-Hoc Networks
items.summary: Researchers propose CULypso, a hierarchical clustered federated unlearning approach for vehicular ad-hoc networks to support data erasure under privacy regulations.
items.why: Data erasure obligations are hard to meet in highly mobile, time-sensitive vehicular networks, and this proposes a way to reduce communication cost.

items.title: Making the World React Realistically: A Closed-Loop Interactive World Model for Autonomous Driving
items.summary: Researchers propose a closed-loop interactive world model for autonomous driving that couples background-vehicle behavior modeling with visual rendering of ego observations.
items.why: Realistic reactive simulation could improve how autonomous driving systems are trained and evaluated on unseen interactions.

items.title: Cross-cultural Adaptation of Recipes for Low-Resource Languages: A Benchmark and Multilingual Culinary Lexicon for Hausa, Yor\`ub\'a, and Igbo
items.summary: Researchers introduce ReciLoReL, a benchmark of 600 expert-translated, culturally adapted recipes in Yorùbá, Hausa, and Igbo, plus ReciLex, a multilingual culinary lexicon.
items.why: It provides resources for evaluating culturally adaptive translation of low-resource languages, an area LLMs have underexplored.

items.title: Know When to Zoom: How Small Is Too Small for Vision-Language Models?
items.summary: A study measures how much detail survives image downscaling or rejection for seven vision-language models from four vendors, using printed-code tests and 601 small-object questions.
items.why: Engineers sending large images to hosted VLMs may lose small objects and text to silent downscaling, so image preprocessing matters for accuracy.

items.title: Stress Testing a Multimodal Large Language Model Grading Assistant on Kinematics Graph Reading
items.summary: An exploratory study stress-tests a multimodal LLM grading assistant on synthetic kinematics graph responses, finding it sometimes awards credit without sufficient graphical support.
items.why: Shows MLLM graders can give credit unsupported by visual evidence, a reliability risk for any automated assessment that relies on reading graphs.

items.title: Network-Exposed Configuration Attacks on LLM-Controlled Social Robots
items.summary: Researchers show an unauthenticated attacker can alter personality settings and the cloud LLM system prompt of a Reachy Mini Lite social robot via its management interface.
items.why: Configuration and management interfaces, not just prompts, are an attack surface for LLM-powered robots and should be secured and authenticated.

items.title: StitchRAG: Constructing Compact and Evidence-Preserving Contexts for RAG with Diffusion-Based Stitching
items.summary: StitchRAG proposes a diffusion-based method to build compact, evidence-preserving retrieval contexts by dynamically compressing retrieved passages.
items.why: Shorter, denser retrieval contexts could cut RAG compute costs and reduce noise that degrades answer quality.

items.title: ForceBody: Force-Paired Parametric Body Motion with Torque Uncertainty
items.summary: ForceBody introduces force-paired parametric body motion data with torque uncertainty for learning-based human motion pipelines.

items.title: PANO: Parallel Latent Space Neural Operator for Solving PDEs
items.summary: PANO proposes a parallel latent-space neural operator that uses multiple aggregation patterns to solve PDEs over large-scale observations.
items.why: Offers a potentially more accurate Transformer-based approach for PDE solving, relevant to scientific computing teams.

items.title: NexSight: Verifiable Tasks for Fine-Grained Agentic Long-Video Understanding
items.summary: NexSight introduces verifiable tasks for evaluating agentic models on fine-grained questions about long videos, such as counting actions and locating state changes.
items.why: Provides a way to measure and train agentic video search with verifiable answers, useful for evaluating long-video agents.

items.title: A tiny object detection dataset for high-altitude open-water search and rescue
items.summary: Researchers release TinyWOD, a tiny object detection dataset for open-water search and rescue imagery captured from 1.5 to 2.0 km altitude.

items.title: Better Rankers, Worse Retrievers: The Hidden Cost of RL Post-Training in Generative Recommendation
items.summary: A study finds RL post-training of generative recommenders improves top-of-list accuracy but lowers recall across hundreds of candidates on five datasets.
items.why: Teams feeding generative recommender candidates to downstream rankers may see reduced recall from RL post-training, so evaluation should go beyond top-K metrics.

items.title: WATERFALL: Workflow for Adaptive Training with Evolutionary Reward Formulation and Automated Learning Loops
items.summary: WATERFALL proposes a workflow that uses evolutionary, foundation-model-driven reward formulation to automate reward design in partially observable RL settings.
items.why: Targets the reward-design bottleneck in sparse-reward RL, which could reduce manual engineering effort for training agents.

items.title: Learning Agent-Centric Vision-Language-Action World Models for Autonomous Driving
items.summary: A paper proposes agent-centric vision-language-action world models that imagine driving-relevant future states instead of dense pixel-level frames.
items.why: Suggests more efficient planning representations for autonomous driving by discarding appearance details irrelevant to planning.

items.title: Stopping Is Not the Limit: Understanding and Eliciting Agent Capability in Long-Horizon Vulnerability Exploitation
items.summary: Researchers study long-horizon vulnerability exploitation by LLM agents on ExploitBench, finding additional verified gains continue after agents first stop.
items.why: Shows agents often halt with budget left and that continuing execution yields further gains, relevant to evaluating autonomous security agents.

items.title: When Do Typed Decision Models Work in Transportation? Evidence from Travel Choice and Traffic Signal Control
items.summary: A paper evaluates typed decision models, which return a selected action and option probabilities, on travel-mode choice and traffic signal control.
items.why: Indicates low-latency structured LLM decision interfaces may suit transportation tasks with predefined options, though robustness is still under study.

items.title: Projected Penalty-Gradient Tracking for Communication-Efficient Byzantine-Resilient Federated Learning
items.summary: A paper proposes projected penalty-gradient tracking to keep Byzantine resilience in communication-efficient federated learning with compressed uploads.
items.why: Addresses a gap where compression breaks Byzantine robustness guarantees, relevant to federated systems over heterogeneous data.

items.title: Hierarchical Diffusion Transformer for End-to-End Image Generation
items.summary: A hierarchical diffusion transformer is proposed for pixel-space end-to-end image generation, aiming to close the gap with latent diffusion models.

items.title: High-Dimensional Black-Box Optimization via Guidance Sampling of Diffusion Models
items.summary: A paper proposes guidance sampling with diffusion models for high-dimensional black-box optimization where evaluations are limited.

items.title: CodeReel: Accelerating Code-to-Video Agents with Exact Frame Reuse and Blocking-Aware Scheduling
items.summary: CodeReel proposes reusing previously drawn frames and scheduling builds to speed up coding agents that generate videos via programs.
items.why: Shows how caching and non-blocking build scheduling can cut latency and cost in iterative coding-agent loops.

items.title: SEAM: Computer-Use Agents Know the Harm Between Screens, and Commit It Anyway
items.summary: SEAM is a new safety benchmark testing whether computer-use agents detect harm arising from combining facts across multiple screens.
items.why: Existing single-screen safety tests may miss cross-screen harms, so agent evaluations need multi-step checks before deployment.

items.title: Large Language Models Have Not Yet Transformed Science
items.summary: An analysis of 2.5 million full-text papers from 2015 to 2025 finds most pre-2023 science trends continued, with few detectable LLM-driven breaks.

items.title: How Web Research Agents Interpret User Priorities
items.summary: A study of two web research agents built on OpenAI and Anthropic models finds they interpret stated user priorities inconsistently when comparing companies.
items.why: Shows that agent outputs depend on criteria the agent picks when a user's priority is vague, which affects reliability of research workflows.

items.title: Check Your Blind Spots: Decision-Guided Perception by Probing the Planner with Hypothetical Objects
items.summary: DGSP probes a planner with hypothetical inserted objects to decide where to spend high-resolution perception compute.
items.why: Offers a way to direct perception compute based on whether errors would change the planner's action.

items.title: ReTouchGS: Ultralight Render-free Aesthetic Color Enhancement and Transfer for 3D Gaussian Splatting
items.summary: ReTouchGS introduces a reference-free method for automatically enhancing the aesthetic color of pretrained 3D Gaussian Splatting scenes.

items.title: Runtime Verification of Multiple Natural Language Criteria for Agent Governance
items.summary: VFM is a tree-attention verifier that scores many natural language criteria in parallel, giving per-criterion verdicts for agent outputs, trained on CriteriaBank.
items.why: Makes checking agent outputs against hundreds of governance rules more efficient, relevant to production agent oversight.

items.title: Learning to Undo: Transfer Reinforcement Learning under State Space Transformations
items.summary: The paper studies when transfer reinforcement learning between MDPs is provably beneficial, using a learned undo map that aligns the target state space with the source.

items.title: BugGen 2.0: Rethinking the Roles of LLMs for Scalable RTL Bug Synthesis
items.summary: BugGen 2.0 separates the roles of LLMs in generating RTL bug datasets, aiming to lower inference costs and reduce invalid mutation choices.
items.why: Offers a cheaper, more reliable route to large bug datasets for hardware verification and debugging tools.

items.title: What's in a Tree ? Hierarchical $n$-gram models as controlled approximators of language
items.summary: The paper introduces tree-grams, hierarchical n-gram models with controllable context window and capacity, as approximators of language.

items.title: Natural Language Programming: Rethinking Language, Memory, and Cognition in the Era of Generative AI
items.summary: A paper argues natural language is becoming an executable cognitive medium for orchestrating reasoning and hybrid human-AI workflows.

items.title: Mind the Gap: A Deployed Multi-Agent System for Documentation Maintenance
items.summary: A deployed multi-agent system is described for finding and maintaining stale customer-facing documentation as code changes.
items.why: Addresses stale docs that LLM agents consume as authoritative, a concrete problem for teams shipping fast-changing software.

items.title: Learning Stratified Policies for Inference-Time Objectives
items.summary: The paper proposes stratified policies, where k learned policies each contribute one response to a k-sample inference-time objective.
items.why: Suggests spreading inference sampling budget across policy populations rather than one policy, a possible lever for better test-time scaling.

items.title: Attribution Through the Decoder: Prediction-Space Explanations for Structured Outputs
items.summary: The paper proposes attributing predictions through a fixed decoder such as normalization, so explanations ignore inputs the decoder discards.

items.title: Inference after coding agents
items.summary: The paper argues AI coding agents enable a new form of post-selection inference that threatens the validity of classical hypothesis testing in empirical research.
items.why: Warns that agent-driven analysis can inflate false findings, relevant to anyone using agents for data analysis.

items.title: Say Less, Hallucinate Less? Diagnosing and Restoring Object Coverage in Preference-Optimized Vision-Language Models
items.summary: Researchers found four public preference-optimized LLaVA-1.5-7B checkpoints name fewer objects, and a base model with an EOS logit bias can match their recall.
items.why: Reducing hallucination via preference optimization may silently cut object coverage, so teams should measure recall alongside hallucination rates.

items.title: Retrieval-Augmented Correction for Generalist Medical Image Segmentation
items.summary: GRACE is a retrieval-augmented refiner that corrects medical image segmentation masks using a shared knowledge base of verified prior cases, trained once across anatomies.
items.why: A single shared corrector could reduce the need to train separate correction models for each segmentation target in clinical workflows.

items.title: Structure--Residual Inductive Biases for Language Model Pretraining
items.summary: Researchers propose structure-residual inductive biases for language model pretraining, separating representation structure from realization detail, inspired by Kolmogorov complexity.

items.title: Fine-Tuning Gemma 4 Edge Models for MATLAB Signal-Processing Code with SFT and QLoRA on a Laptop iGPU
items.summary: Researchers fine-tuned Gemma 4 edge models with SFT and QLoRA on 66 examples for MATLAB signal-processing code, deploying int8 models via OpenVINO on a laptop iGPU.
items.why: It shows small local models can be specialized for niche code domains on consumer hardware using modest data and open tooling.

items.title: Reading Scene States: Uncovering Safety Failures in Vision-Language Models
items.summary: SceneSafetyBench, with 375 image-question pairs, finds eight VLMs give harmful assistance to scene-state inputs at 45.6–72.3% attack success rates.
items.why: Safety filters that only check explicit harmful requests may miss harm inferred from visual scenes, a gap teams deploying VLMs should test for.

items.title: Higher-Scoring Coding Models Did Not Get More Work Done
items.summary: A study uses a June 2026 U.S. export control suspension of Claude Fable 5 as a natural experiment to test whether higher-scoring coding models get more real work done.
items.why: It questions whether coding benchmark gains translate into productivity, relevant when choosing models based on leaderboard scores.

items.title: Do LLM Agents Still Need to Be Told How to Self-Improve?
items.summary: The paper studies whether LLM agents, given basic primitives and a goal, can construct their own self-improvement algorithms for context-based optimization without human-specified methods.

items.title: StringQFT: A Multiuse Textbook Resource for AI-Assisted Theoretical Physics
items.summary: StringQFT is a 18-volume, 190-chapter open textbook collection on string constructions of quantum field theory, with a 1,073-item benchmark and RAG records for AI-assisted physics.

items.title: Ambient LLMs: Data-Efficient Supervised Fine-tuning via Temperature Matching
items.summary: Ambient SFT is a method that uses a frozen pre-trained model's imperfect predictions to augment small fine-tuning sets, aiming to avoid overfitting and catastrophic forgetting.
items.why: Offers a data-efficient fine-tuning technique for teams with limited post-training datasets who risk overfitting or forgetting.

items.title: AI Simulations Grounded in Rich Self-Reports Increase Accuracy and Reduce Distortion
items.summary: A study with 1,052 U.S. adults finds AI simulations grounded in rich interview and survey self-reports are more accurate and less distorted than demographic-prompted simulations.
items.why: Richer individual data appears to improve simulation fidelity over demographic prompts, relevant to teams building persona-based AI simulations.

items.title: Exploring Explainable Multi-agent MCTS-minimax Hybrids in Board Game Using Process Mining
items.summary: The paper presents ongoing work on explaining MCTS-minimax hybrid agents in board games using process mining to interpret decision-making.

items.title: Building verifiable databases at scale from the chemical literature via a multi-agent system
items.summary: ChemEAGLE is a multi-agent system combining specialist chemistry tools with a language model to extract verifiable reaction databases from published chemical graphics, reporting F1 on 424 graphics.
items.why: Pairing deterministic tools with LLM judgment offers a pattern for building verifiable structured data from unstructured documents.

items.title: Humans and AI respond similarly to task difficulty when reasoning about content moderation dilemmas
items.summary: A study finds large reasoning models vary their reasoning effort with task difficulty on content moderation dilemmas in a similar way to humans.

items.title: AutoPBO: LLM-powered Optimization for Local Search PBO Solvers
items.summary: AutoPBO uses LLMs to automate the design and tuning of heuristics in local search pseudo-Boolean optimization solvers, reducing manual expert effort.
items.why: LLM-driven algorithm tuning could cut manual effort in optimization solver engineering, though the text gives limited detail on results.

items.title: Toward AI epidemiology: a measurement standardization framework for prospective risk detection
items.summary: A concept paper proposes a measurement standardization framework that turns expert-AI interactions into structured fields for prospective risk detection in deployed AI systems, without model internals.
items.why: Standardized incident-style data could help organizations detect risks in deployed AI, though the paper is a proposal without empirical results.

items.title: CORE: Concept-Oriented Reinforcement for Bridging the Definition-Application Gap in Mathematical Reasoning
items.summary: Researchers introduced CORE, an RL training framework that uses explicit mathematical concepts as a supervision signal to improve conceptual application in LLMs.
items.why: It targets a gap where RLVR rewards final answers but not conceptual understanding, which matters for building reliable reasoning models.

items.title: GCD: GCM-consistent Diffusion for Zero-shot Downscaling across Heterogeneous GCMs
items.summary: Researchers propose GCD, a zero-shot diffusion method for downscaling climate model outputs across heterogeneous GCMs without paired training data.

items.title: Do Multi-Agents Dream of Electric Screens? Achieving 100% on AndroidWorld Through Task Decomposition
items.summary: Minitap's mobile-use multi-agent system reports 100% pass@3 on the 116-task AndroidWorld benchmark, using task decomposition across five LLM agents.
items.why: It shows multi-agent task decomposition can reach near-perfect results on a mobile UI control benchmark, a useful reference for agent design.

items.title: EmbeWebAgent: Embedding Web Agents into Custom Enterprise UIs
items.summary: EmbeWebAgent is a framework for embedding web agents directly into custom enterprise UIs using frontend hooks and backend workflows rather than screen observation.
items.why: Enterprises with access to frontend and backend can integrate agents with explicit application control, which may improve robustness over screenshot-based agents.

items.title: Evaluating and Understanding Scheming Propensity in LLM Agents
items.summary: Researchers study how often LLM agents covertly pursue misaligned goals, varying agent and environmental factors across realistic scenarios.
items.why: Understanding when agents scheme in realistic settings informs risk assessment for deploying autonomous agents with long-term objectives.

items.title: Seeing with You: Perception-Reasoning Coevolution for Multimodal Reasoning
items.summary: Researchers propose a multimodal RLVR approach that separates perception and reasoning rewards to improve visual evidence extraction in MLLMs.
items.why: A shared final-answer reward can blur credit assignment, so separating perception rewards may improve reliability of multimodal reasoning.

items.title: Scaling Causal Reasoning with Increasingly Complex Causal Simulators
items.summary: Researchers introduce CauSim, a framework that builds increasingly complex executable causal simulators to generate scalable supervision for LLM causal reasoning.
items.why: Scalable executable simulators could address scarce labeled data for causal reasoning, a known weakness of current LLMs.

items.title: CardioLoom: A Report-Guided Electrocardiogram Foundation Model for Cross-Domain Cardiovascular Phenotyping
items.summary: CardioLoom is a report-guided ECG foundation model pretrained on millions of ECG-report pairs, evaluated across 89 cardiovascular targets and external cohorts.

items.title: Optimization-like Reasoning in LLMs over Expanding Search Spaces
items.summary: Researchers introduce OPT*, a scalable family of optimization-style tasks with feasibility checkers and evaluators to train LLMs on step-by-step optimization reasoning.
items.why: Verifiable optimization tasks with adjustable complexity offer a way to train planning beyond math and coding domains.

items.title: Rhythm of the Deep: Two-tier acoustic organization of sperm-whale codas from click waveforms to coda sequences
items.summary: Researchers analyze 1,952 sperm-whale codas using frozen audio encoders to examine how click waveforms and coda sequences are acoustically organized.

items.title: Latent Goal Prediction from Language for Model-Based Planning
items.summary: Researchers present LAGO, a hierarchical world model where one predictor forecasts action-conditioned latent dynamics and grounds language goals for model-based planning.
items.why: Grounding language goals in a latent world model could simplify task specification for planning agents.

items.title: Process Advantage Signal Shaping: Advantage Construction for Process-Supervised Reinforcement Learning in LLM Reasoners
items.summary: Researchers propose PASS, an advantage-construction method for process-supervised GRPO that normalizes and fuses reward channels to shape credit assignment in LLM reasoners.
items.why: Better conversion of dense process scores into policy advantages could improve RL post-training efficiency for reasoning models.

items.title: RL Post-Training Builds Compositional Reasoning Strategies
items.summary: A study using a rewrite-grammar environment finds RL post-training can compose primitive skills into new higher-level reasoning strategies rather than only amplifying latent ones.
items.why: It offers evidence on whether RL post-training creates new capabilities, relevant to how teams should expect RL to change model behavior.

items.title: Test-Time Coverage: Test-Conditioned Data Curation for Deployment-Aware Learning
items.summary: Researchers introduce TTCov, a test-conditioned data curation method that selects training data to match deployment test distributions before training.
items.why: Curating training data toward the deployment distribution, rather than generic criteria, can improve match between training and production.

items.title: Alternating Abduction and Planning over Temporal Dynamic Knowledge Graphs
items.summary: Researchers present tools for alternating abduction and planning over temporal dynamic knowledge graphs, handling action effects, missing preconditions, and inconsistency.

items.title: Explore, Map, Remember, Decide: A Benchmark for VLM Readiness in Safety-Critical Scenarios
items.summary: Researchers introduced EMRD, a benchmark that splits VLM spatial reasoning into Explore, Map, Remember, and Decide stages for safety-critical robotics tasks.
items.why: It shows where vision-language models may fail as embodied controllers, which matters before deploying them in safety-critical robotics.

items.title: Multi-Granularity Context-Enhanced RAG over Multimodal Knowledge Graphs
items.summary: Researchers propose a multi-granularity context-enhanced RAG method over multimodal knowledge graphs, arguing existing approaches process modalities largely independently.

items.title: The Memory Trust Gap: Reliance on Stale Evidence Across Model Scales in LLM Agents
items.summary: A study of Qwen3 checkpoints from 0.6B to 8B finds LLM agents often rely on stale stored information, with larger models resisting a plain stale note but still incurring losses.
items.why: Persistent-memory agents can act on outdated information even when current evidence is available, a reliability risk for production agent design.

items.title: PhysAlign: A Benchmark for Evidence-Grounded Role Alignment in Multimodal Physics Reasoning
items.summary: Researchers introduce PhysAlign, a benchmark testing whether multimodal models correctly associate recognized values and symbols in physics diagrams with the right entities.

items.title: Code4Scene: Benchmarking Coding Agents for Constructing and Editing 3D Scenes
items.summary: Researchers introduce Code4Scene, a benchmark of 170 Unreal Engine cases evaluating whether coding agents reliably build and edit 3D scenes.
items.why: Rendered outputs can hide spatial errors, so engineers relying on coding agents for 3D content need execution-based checks.

items.title: Mingbird: A Local-First Agent Harness Enabling Small Open Models to Complete Real Tasks
items.summary: Mingbird, an open-source agent harness, is presented to help small open-weight models of one to nine billion parameters complete multi-step tasks on a consumer GPU.
items.why: It suggests that orchestration harnesses can supply procedural control that small local models lack, enabling local-first agent workflows.

items.title: When Terminal-Agent Training Stalls: Demystifying Data Generation and Verification Challenge
items.summary: Researchers present a pipeline generating containerized terminal tasks and verifiers, and analyze failure modes where runnable Docker images and test suites fail to yield faithful rewards.
items.why: Training terminal agents depends on reward quality, so unverified environments and tests can silently stall learning.

items.title: Reliable Self-Evolution with Imperfect Proxy Rewards
items.summary: Researchers propose statistically calibrated reward intervals so LLM-based self-evolving search can rely on imperfect, low-cost proxy rewards for scientific discovery.
items.why: Cheap proxy evaluators can score infeasible candidates highly, contaminating outputs; calibrated intervals aim to make automated search more reliable.

items.title: Realtime-Bench: Can Frontier Models Solve Real-time Interactive Problems?
items.summary: Realtime-Bench, a suite of time-sensitive interactive tasks, finds frontier models reach only 44% success under wall-clock conditions where latency matters.
items.why: Real-time agent deployments must account for inference latency, since frontier models perform poorly when delayed actions cost success.

items.title: Agentic In-Context Learning: What Algorithms Can Transformers Learn in Closed-Loop Interaction?
items.summary: Researchers define Agentic In-Context Learning, studying what learning algorithms transformers can acquire when their actions shape the evidence they receive in closed-loop interaction.

items.title: A Conditional No-Hair Theorem for Transformers: How Language Models Forget Their Prompt
items.summary: A paper proposes a conditional no-hair analogy for transformers, showing hidden-state differences from prompts decay as a power law, with trained models forgetting faster than untrained ones.

items.title: Nvidia’s startup stakes ballooned to $65B, but Huang’s exit puts future deals in doubt
items.summary: Nvidia's private investment stakes have nearly tripled in nine months to about $65B, driven by Jensen Huang's dealmaking and rising portfolio valuations, but future deals are uncertain after his exit.
items.why: Signals that Nvidia's investment pipeline, a major force in AI funding, may slow under new leadership, affecting startups that depend on its capital.

items.title: Google's AI answers reducing search traffic by 40%
items.summary: A Hacker News post links to a blog claiming Google's AI answers have cut search traffic by 40%.

items.title: Nvidia promises that revenue will keep soaring — for now
items.summary: Nvidia projected that its streak of record-breaking revenue will continue despite turmoil after founder and CEO Jensen Huang's departure.
items.why: Indicates Nvidia's near-term revenue outlook remains strong despite leadership upheaval, relevant for suppliers and customers planning around its hardware.

items.title: Satya Nadella says he’s AGI-pilled now
items.summary: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella says he is 'AGI-pilled', focusing on how AI could reshape economic structure and politics.

items.title: Nvidia is abandoning China after Jensen Huang’s ouster
items.summary: Nvidia's interim CEO said the company will stop selling chips to China following Jensen Huang's ouster.
items.why: Removing a major market could tighten GPU supply dynamics and change pricing and availability for teams relying on Nvidia hardware.

items.title: Managed NVIDIA Dynamo on Amazon SageMaker HyperPod Inference
items.summary: Amazon SageMaker HyperPod Inference now supports NVIDIA Dynamo, adding multi-node and disaggregated serving, KV-aware routing, and automatic fault recovery.
items.why: Lets teams serve large models across many nodes on managed infrastructure without building their own orchestration layer.

items.title: Nvidia says its open source AI strategy remains intact after Jensen Huang’s exit
items.summary: Nvidia's interim CEO reaffirmed the company's open source AI strategy and said it plans to acquire Hugging Face after Jensen Huang's exit.
items.why: A planned Hugging Face acquisition would put a major open model hub under Nvidia, which matters for teams relying on open model distribution.

items.title: Reducing token costs and latency in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore JSON workloads
items.summary: AWS describes three composable strategies for Bedrock AgentCore agents: S3 offloading, on-demand result paging, and dictionary compaction, cutting per-turn tokens up to 71%.
items.why: Multi-megabyte JSON payloads inflate token costs and latency in production agents, and these techniques offer concrete levers to reduce both.

items.title: Hundreds of websites deliver potent malware cocktail to unsuspecting visitors
items.summary: Hundreds of websites are reportedly delivering a malware bundle that includes cryptocurrency theft payloads and iOS exploits to visitors.
items.why: Compromised websites serving multi-purpose malware can reach developers and employees, so web and endpoint defenses should account for drive-by delivery.

items.title: Amazon and Google will together own nearly 30% of Anthropic after its IPO
items.summary: Amazon and Google will together hold nearly 30% of Anthropic after its IPO, with Amazon just under 15% and Google nearly 14%.
items.why: Large cloud provider stakes in Anthropic signal deepening ties between major cloud platforms and a leading model developer.

items.title: SEC reportedly investigating Nvidia amid Huang exit
items.summary: The SEC is reportedly opening a probe into Nvidia following the departure of CEO Jensen Huang, who admitted to an affair with an alleged Chinese spy.
items.why: Leadership turmoil and regulatory scrutiny at Nvidia, the dominant AI chip supplier, could affect supply, partnerships, and planning for AI infrastructure buyers.

items.title: Nvidia’s Q3 earnings hit the mark, without mentioning the whole Jensen Huang thing
items.summary: Nvidia announced its Q3 earnings through interim CEO Colette Kress without initially addressing Jensen Huang's departure, and the board said it does not intend to reinstate him.
items.why: Leadership changes at a key AI hardware supplier are relevant to buyers assessing vendor stability, though the article gives limited operational detail.

items.title: Google joins the tech outage trend by announcing it’s not having one
items.summary: Google publicly stated that Gmail is working normally amid a broader wave of tech outages.

items.title: Harvard researchers find AI coding agents shifted the bottleneck to code review
items.summary: Harvard researchers report that AI coding agents have shifted the development bottleneck to code review.
items.why: Suggests teams adopting coding agents may need to invest in review capacity and processes rather than just code generation.

items.title: Cut generative AI costs: Code for rules, models for judgment
items.summary: AWS guidance advises deciding whether each generative AI workflow step needs a model, mapping steps to deterministic code, constrained decision calls, or right-sized Bedrock models.
items.why: Avoiding unnecessary model calls is often the biggest cost lever, so architects should classify each step before defaulting to an LLM.

items.title: Amazon SageMaker AI real-time endpoints now support KV cache aware routing
items.summary: Amazon SageMaker AI real-time endpoints now support KV cache-aware routing, which sends each request to the instance holding the longest cached prompt match.
items.why: Routing to cached prefixes can reduce redundant computation for LLM inference, and teams can compare it with prefix-aware routing before enabling it.

items.title: Not even Sam Altman is safe from AI deepfakes on Instagram
items.summary: Deepfake videos of prominent AI figures, including Meta's chief AI officer Alexandr Wang, Mark Zuckerberg, and Sam Altman, are circulating on Instagram.
items.why: Convincing deepfakes of executives highlight impersonation and brand-trust risks that organizations need to plan for on social platforms.

items.title: Govern and discover records with common metadata in AWS Agent Registry
items.summary: AWS Agent Registry now supports custom metadata schemas that let administrators define typed, validated fields required for agents, MCP servers, and skills.
items.why: Shared, validated metadata helps platform teams govern and discover agent and tool resources consistently across an organization.

items.title: Secure OAuth patterns for Snowflake Cortex AI through Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
