items.summary: VibeSyn is an intent-driven system where hierarchical agents translate chemist-defined goals into multistep molecule synthesis plans that can be revised as evidence accumulates.
items.why: Demonstrates hierarchical agent design for long-horizon scientific workflows that need revisable decisions rather than hard-coded pipelines.

items.title: An LLM-assisted theoretical model for aeroengine installation noise scattering
items.summary: Researchers present an analytical model chaining two Wiener–Hopf problems to study aeroengine fan noise scattering off a nearby semi-infinite rigid plate.
items.why: Offers a theoretical tool for predicting aircraft installation noise, relevant mainly to acoustics and aerospace engineers rather than AI practitioners.

items.title: Accelerating Variational Cone-Beam CT Reconstruction with Learned Warm Starts
items.summary: Researchers propose a neural network-guided warm-start framework to speed up variational cone-beam CT reconstruction while keeping the explicit acquisition model and priors.
items.why: Shows learned initialization can cut iterative optimization cost without replacing the variational formulation, a useful pattern for imaging pipelines.

items.title: LEAP-LLM: Preserving lead-time structure for question-conditioned ECG interpretation
items.summary: LEAP-LLM is proposed to make ECG interpretation by LLMs question-conditioned and preserve lead-time structure instead of encoding the ECG independently of the clinical question.
items.why: Suggests query-aware encoding and per-lead structure can improve medical signal-language models, relevant to teams building clinical LLM systems.

items.title: CARET: Clinical Assertion-Aware Residual Calibration for Medical Image-Text Alignment
items.summary: CARET is introduced as a parameter-efficient image-side adaptation method that uses paired positive and negative clinical statements to calibrate medical image-text alignment.
items.why: Addresses how negation and uncertainty in radiology reports can distort vision-language predictions, a practical risk for medical AI deployments.

items.title: RescueVLM: Model-Agnostic Vision-Language Framework for Rescue Drone Imagery
items.summary: RescueVLM is a model-agnostic vision-language framework for triaging rescue drone imagery on-premises, avoiding cloud services due to GDPR and civil-protection rules.
items.why: Illustrates how data-residency constraints push vision-language systems toward local, model-swappable architectures in regulated public-safety settings.

items.title: Foundation Model Fine-Tuning with Attention-based Multi-View Fusion for Multi-Task Cardiac Function Assessment
items.summary: Researchers propose a multi-task framework using foundation model fine-tuning and attention-based multi-view fusion to assess cardiac function from echocardiography.
items.why: Shows multi-view fusion on foundation models for standardizing a clinically operator-dependent measurement, relevant to medical imaging ML teams.

items.title: What to Practice Next? Latent Profile-Guided Task Selection for Skill-Evolving LLM Agents
items.summary: SPG-Select is a framework that chooses LLM agent practice tasks using a multidimensional skill profile inferred via MIRT and predicted surrogate progress.
items.why: Offers a method for adaptive task scheduling in agent training, though its practical impact depends on results not given in the summary.

items.title: KUDEX: A Zero-Shot Decompositional Framework for Logical Analysis in Natural Language
items.summary: KUDEX is a zero-shot framework that decomposes natural-language reasoning into atomic primitives and builds reasoning graphs to verify logical relationships.
items.why: Provides a transparent, zero-shot way to check multi-step LLM reasoning, which may help teams audit model logic.

items.title: Self-Improvement Memory Enables Continual Recursive Self-Improvement
items.summary: Researchers study Continual Recursive Self-Improvement and propose Self-Improvement Memory, which stores harness-optimizer history to reuse edits across benchmarks or policy models.
items.why: Suggests optimizers that remember why past edits were made can transfer harness improvements when benchmarks or models change.

items.title: The opposing informational effects of AI trading
items.summary: A paper argues that better AI forecasting can reduce the private information aggregated into prices, while trades can also convey public-data analysis to others.
items.why: Highlights that improved AI in markets can have opposing effects on price informativeness, relevant to quantitative finance and market design.

items.title: Label-Free Detection of Structural Bias in LLM-Based Recommender Systems via Randomized Paraphrasing: The Case of Verbosity
items.summary: A label-free framework is proposed to audit LLM-based recommenders for structural biases such as preference for longer product descriptions, using randomized paraphrasing.
items.why: Offers a way to detect verbosity bias in LLM recommenders without relevance labels, useful for teams running e-commerce ranking with LLMs.

items.title: We Have All the Cards: Securing Agent Cards at the Operational Trust Boundary of the Agent2Agent Protocol
items.summary: The paper characterizes ten Agent Card manipulation attacks in the Agent2Agent protocol and presents SECCARD, a layered validation framework for securing agent metadata.
items.why: Agent discovery metadata can be attacker-controlled and influence selection before invocation, so teams adopting A2A need validation layers.

items.title: Benchmark Factory: Agentic Benchmark Creation via Dataset Curation and Label-Free Quality Anchors
items.summary: Benchmark Factory is an autonomous meta-agent loop that builds coding-agent benchmarks from a team's production code changes, using label-free quality anchors and human checkpoints.
items.why: Lets teams create validated evaluation sets from their own codebase, reducing the risk of misleading benchmarks for coding agents.

items.title: Lasso: Towards Sustainable AI-Generated Media Detection with Intel QAT On-Chip Compression
items.summary: Researchers reverse engineer Intel QuickAssist compression accelerator microarchitecture and build Lasso, a hardware-assisted detector for AI-generated media.
items.why: Shows hardware compression accelerators can be repurposed to make AI-generated content detection cheaper and more power-efficient at scale.

items.title: The Human Side of ML Engineering: Analyzing the Collaboration and Communication Skills in ML Job Postings
items.summary: An analysis of 1,000 job postings (500 ML, 500 SE) examines demand for collaboration and communication skills across regions, industries, and seniority levels.
items.why: Indicates how employers express soft-skill demand for ML roles versus software engineering, useful for hiring and career planning.

items.title: Effects of Conventional, Adaptive, and AI-Powered Upscaling on the Legibility of License Plates
items.summary: Researchers ran two online experiments measuring how well humans can read license plates of 8 to 128 pixels tall under conventional, adaptive, and AI-powered upscaling.
items.why: It tests whether AI upscaling that synthesizes detail actually helps human readers versus explainable interpolation, relevant to trust in enhancement tools.

items.title: From Language-Specific to Cross-DSL: Semantic-Role-Guided Model Completion with LLMs
items.summary: Researchers introduce RAFiC, an LLM-based approach for iterative domain model completion that generalizes across domain-specific languages using semantic roles.

items.title: Context Matters: Improving LLM-Based Code Summarization with Hierarchical Information
items.summary: Researchers propose enriching source code documentation with hierarchical context so LLMs can summarize code better despite limited context windows.
items.why: Hierarchical context may improve LLM code summaries and documentation quality for developers working on large codebases.

items.title: Probing Where Surprise Happens: Localized Violation-of-Expectation Evaluation of Video World Models
items.summary: Researchers introduce localized violation-of-expectation evaluation to test whether video world models detect physically impossible events at the specific locations and times they occur.
items.why: Aggregate benchmarks can mask where video models fail physically, so localized evaluation gives teams a finer-grained way to assess world models.

items.title: Model Maps: A Documentation Framework for Tracing Foundation Model Ancestry and Understanding AI Entanglement
items.summary: Researchers propose Model Maps, a documentation framework for tracing foundation model ancestry and the upstream artifacts that shape downstream model behavior.
items.why: Tracing upstream models, datasets, and benchmarks can expose inherited security, hallucination, and bias risks in AI supply chains.

items.title: Agent-ZTA: A chain-Aware Zero Trust Model for Bidirectional Security-State Propagation and Runtime Containment in Multi-Agent Delegation
items.summary: Researchers present Agent-ZTA, a zero trust authorization model that tracks security-state changes during runtime across chains of delegating multi-agent systems.
items.why: Static caller-based authorization misses mid-execution compromise in agent delegation chains, so runtime containment matters for securing multi-agent deployments.

items.title: Role-Separated Diffusion Transformers: Global Rule Isolation and Deterministic Sampling Manifold Compression
items.summary: Researchers present Role-Separated Diffusion Transformers, an architecture that isolates a global rule from image tokens to improve class-conditional diffusion models.

items.title: MemoryLane: Supporting Reminiscence Conversations Between Older Adults with Mild Dementia and Lay Caregivers Using a Simulated AI Agent
items.summary: Researchers present MemoryLane, a system using a simulated AI agent to support reminiscence conversations between older adults with mild dementia and lay caregivers.

items.title: HeteroWear: Sensor-Aware Self-Supervised Learning for Heterogeneous Wearable Activity Recognition
items.summary: Researchers present HeteroWear, a sensor-aware self-supervised framework pretrained on eight wearable datasets to recognize activity across heterogeneous devices and sensors.
items.why: Testing whether representations transfer across heterogeneous sensor setups helps teams judge whether pretraining, not just architecture, drives wearable model gains.

items.title: SurveyWeave: An Agentic Framework for Automated Survey Generation
items.summary: Researchers present SurveyWeave, an agentic framework that uses three coordinating agents to automatically generate research surveys from large sets of papers.
items.why: Multi-agent review and revision loops for source-faithful long-form generation offer a design pattern for document-heavy agent workflows.

items.title: Refinement vs. Replanning: Inference Compute Allocation in Robot Policies
items.summary: Researchers study how to allocate fixed inference compute in a frozen chunked robot policy between refining action chunks and replanning more frequently.
items.why: Deployment-time compute trade-offs in robot policies affect latency and cost decisions without any retraining of model weights.

items.title: The Critic Can Hurt: On the Safety of Critics in LLM-Guided AutoML Search
items.summary: Researchers audit LLM critics in AutoML search and find a naive 8B critic often drives search below a no-critic random-search baseline on tabular datasets.
items.why: LLM critics in agentic optimization loops can degrade results, so teams should audit whether feedback components help rather than assume they do.

items.title: Understanding the Role of Reasoning Data in Pretraining
items.summary: Researchers study how to balance atomic facts and reasoning traces in pretraining data, using a linear transformer to analyze generalization to unseen transitions.

items.title: More Context, Mixed Results: Evaluating LLMs for Identifier Recovery and Code Deobfuscation
items.summary: Researchers evaluate three LLMs against four traditional baselines on recovering obfuscated Java identifiers across 51 projects, finding mixed results depending on context.
items.why: LLMs generally beat traditional deobfuscation methods, but the benefit depends on context type, informing reverse engineering tool choices.

items.title: Hard or Mislabeled? Failure Screens Enrich Vision Benchmarks for Label Errors
items.summary: Researchers find that images misclassified by all 66 supervised classifiers on ImageNet's validation set are 61% mislabeled, versus 11.1% overall.
items.why: Failure-based benchmark filtering can concentrate label errors, so teams building evaluation sets should verify labels before treating failures as model weaknesses.

items.title: SPARC: Evidence-guided adaptive model composition for materials discovery
items.summary: Researchers introduce SPARC, a framework that continually revises which measurements and model relationships are trusted during closed-loop materials experimentation.
items.why: It offers a method for combining competing models via out-of-fold evaluation, which could inform adaptive experiment design in R&D pipelines.

items.title: Nahual: A Sequence Model for Language and Atoms
items.summary: Researchers propose Nahual, a decoder-only autoregressive diffusion model that aims to combine language control with generation of 3D atomic coordinates.
items.why: It targets controllable molecular generation, a gap where general LLMs handle 3D coordinates poorly and specialist models lack language control.

items.title: Can Agentic LLMs Write Task-Based Parallel Code? A Study of OpenMP Tasking, HPX, StarPU and TTG
items.summary: A study tests how well open-weight LLM agents write C++ task-based parallel code for OpenMP Tasking, HPX, StarPU and TTG using an iterative compile-and-run workflow.
items.why: It shows how agentic coding workflows perform on less common HPC runtimes, relevant to teams using LLM agents for parallel software development.

items.title: ST-GAT: A Leakage-Free Spatio-Temporal Graph Attention Framework for Robust Network Intrusion Detection
items.summary: Researchers propose ST-GAT, a spatio-temporal graph attention network for intrusion detection, and argue that common benchmark evaluations suffer from temporal leakage and preprocessing contamination.
items.why: It highlights evaluation pitfalls that can inflate intrusion detection results, a concern for teams validating security ML models.

items.title: Latency, Speech Recognition and Turn-Taking in Voice Agents for Spanish Phone Negotiation: An Externally Measured Comparison of Pipecat, LiveKit and GPT-Live
items.summary: An externally measured comparison of Pipecat, LiveKit Agents and OpenAI's GPT-Live finds differences in latency, speech recognition and turn-taking for a Spanish phone negotiation voice agent.
items.why: It gives comparative latency and turn-taking data for voice agent architectures, useful when choosing a stack for real-time phone agents.

items.title: DecoEdit: Beyond Flat Control for 3D-Aware Unified Image Editing
items.summary: Researchers present DecoEdit, a unified image editing framework that adds 3D-aware control over object location, scale and orientation while preserving identity.
items.why: It extends image editing beyond flat 2D controls, though the summary gives limited detail on deployment implications.

items.title: Beyond Plain MCP: Do Decision Models and Code Mode Make Tool Use Cheaper and Faster?
items.summary: A preregistered study compares MCP code mode and decision-layer routers against plain MCP for tool use by open-weight agents across up to 1,958 distractor tools.
items.why: It provides evidence on when tool-routing strategies reduce tokens and latency for agents that manage large tool catalogs.

items.title: How Much Determinism Can Fine-Tuning Buy? Margin Regularisation Against Batch-Induced Token Flips
items.summary: Researchers propose margin regularisation during fine-tuning to reduce greedy-decoding token flips caused by batch composition, rather than relying on inference-time fixes.
items.why: Batch-dependent nondeterminism affects reproducibility in production LLM serving, and training-time mitigation could be an alternative to throughput-costly fixes.

items.title: When the Mythical Man-Month Meets Agentic Web Systems: Structured Coordination for Scalable Development
items.summary: The paper examines how adding agents to multi-agent web systems can fail to improve performance due to coordination overhead, and proposes structured coordination to scale them.
items.why: It addresses when adding more agents hurts rather than helps, a practical design concern for teams building multi-agent systems.

items.title: MarineSparkLM-4B: A Lightweight Language Model for Marine and Offshore Engineering Built by Parameter-Efficient Adaptation
items.summary: Researchers adapt a 4-billion-parameter model with two LoRA adapters into MarineSparkLM-4B, a language model for marine and offshore engineering, trained on a single workstation.
items.why: It shows domain adaptation of a small model on modest hardware, though the domain focus limits broader engineering relevance.

items.title: Mean-field Token Steering
items.summary: The paper frames stochastic token steering through transformer layers as a mean-field control problem for interacting tokens on the unit sphere.
items.why: It is a theoretical treatment of transformer dynamics with little immediate engineering application stated in the text.

items.title: Isolating Perception for Multi-View Planning under Occlusion-Induced Partial Observability
items.summary: Researchers introduce BW-PO, a Blocksworld-based benchmark for occlusion-induced partial observability, and propose VLM-as-perceiver, which limits VLMs to local perception and delegates planning to external solvers.
items.why: It shows VLM planners fail under occlusion and that delegating reasoning to external solvers may be a more reliable architecture.

items.title: On-policy distillation as a Backdoor Propagation Channel
items.summary: Researchers show that on-policy distillation can transfer a conditional backdoor implanted in a teacher model into a student model during LLM post-training.
items.why: It reveals a supply-chain risk for teams using distillation from teacher models, since backdoors may propagate to students.

items.title: Neural Dual Bounds: Valid-by-Construction JGLP Warm-Starts for MAP and Constrained MAP
items.summary: Researchers present Neural Dual Bounds, a neural network that produces valid upper bounds for MAP inference in graphical models in a single forward pass to warm-start JGLP.
items.why: It offers a faster route to tight bounds for graphical model inference, though the summary gives limited broader context.

items.title: Revisiting What Makes a Good Context Subset: A Sparse Latent Basis Perspective
items.summary: Researchers study what makes a good few-shot context subset, framing demonstration selection as sparse reconstruction and proposing Residual Explanation Search.
items.why: It gives a principled framing for demonstration selection that may improve few-shot prompt construction in LLM applications.

items.title: Beyond Alignment: Supervising the Generator for EEG-to-Image Reconstruction
items.summary: Researchers argue that stronger EEG-image alignment does not improve reconstruction quality, so the image generator itself needs explicit supervision, proposing Representation Alignment (REPA).
items.why: Suggests that improving conditioning inputs alone may not help generative models, pointing to supervising the generation process directly.

items.title: HospitalBench: Diagnosing Where and Why Embodied Agents Fail on Long Hospital Task Chains
items.summary: HospitalBench is a diagnostic benchmark of ten hospital chores in NVIDIA Isaac Sim, testing where and why vision-language embodied agents fail on causal five-step task chains.
items.why: Shows end-task success hides failure points in long-horizon agent tasks, so teams need step-level diagnostics for embodied agents.

items.title: SAR-TopoGuard: Training-Free, Speckle-Aware Topological Verification for Structure-Preserving SAR-to-Optical Translation
items.summary: SAR-TopoGuard is a training-free inference-time layer that samples candidate outputs from frozen generators and filters them for speckle-aware structure in SAR-to-optical translation.
items.why: Offers a way to reduce hallucinated detail in frozen generative models without retraining, relevant to remote sensing pipelines.

items.title: Generation of protein conformations using a simple inverted transformer
items.summary: Researchers introduce an AI system based on a variant of the Transformer architecture to generate protein conformations, aiming to reduce the compute needed for molecular dynamics sampling.
items.why: Points to deep learning as a cheaper route to protein conformational sampling, though the text gives limited detail on results.

items.title: Benchmarking the State of AI for Crop Yield Forecasting: A Global Assessment Across Modeling Paradigms
items.summary: A global benchmark compares five crop yield forecasting paradigms, including statistical, process-based, machine learning, deep sequence, and tabular foundation models.
items.why: Provides standardized evidence on which modeling approaches work for yield forecasting, though the text gives few specific findings.

items.title: OmitEHR: Scalable Omission Detection in LLM-Generated Clinical Summaries
items.summary: OmitEHR is a reference-free omission detector that learns clinical salience from historical clinician data to find missing information in LLM-generated clinical summaries.
items.why: Targets omissions, reported as the most common LLM failure in clinical summaries, which matters for healthcare AI deployments.

items.title: SMELL: Sparsity-aware Memory Efficient Federated Fine-tuning for Long-context LLMs
items.summary: SMELL is a sparsity-aware, memory-efficient federated fine-tuning framework for long-context LLMs on resource-constrained devices.
items.why: Addresses activation memory, heterogeneous clients, and communication costs for fine-tuning LLMs on distributed private data.

items.title: Pixel-KWS: Rendered-Glyph Representations for Orthographically Robust Open-Vocabulary Keyword Spotting
items.summary: PIXEL-KWS represents characters as rendered glyph images rather than learned embeddings, enabling open-vocabulary keyword spotting that handles homoglyphs and unseen symbols.
items.why: Offers a robustness approach for keyword spotting with user-defined keywords that involve unusual or visually similar characters.

items.title: Do Pretraining Optimizer Gains Transfer to KL Distillation?
items.summary: Comparison of AdamW, AdaGrad, Shampoo variants, SOAP, and All-2D Muon across Qwen student-teacher pairs finds none consistently improves KL distillation trade-offs over elementwise baselines.
items.why: Suggests matrix-structured pretraining optimizers may not justify their cost for short-horizon distillation runs.

items.title: Prepare Lighter and Faster for Open-Vocabulary Queries: A Query-Wise 3D Segmenter for Gaussian Splatting
items.summary: A lightweight, training-free framework performs query-driven 3D instance segmentation on Gaussian Splatting using dense pixel-level CLIP features instead of mask-wise embeddings.
items.why: Reduces preprocessing and training cost for open-vocabulary 3D segmentation, useful for fast 3D scene understanding pipelines.

items.title: Do Rule-Based Tools Help LLMs Translate Endangered Uralic Languages in the Prompt or over MCP?
items.summary: A manual evaluation tests whether giving LLMs rule-based linguistic resources for four endangered Uralic languages improves translation, comparing prompt-embedded analyses with MCP tool calls.
items.why: Compares two integration methods for supplying tools to LLMs, relevant to how teams expose external resources via MCP.

items.title: CLEW: Log-Anchored Backward Tracing for Root-Cause Code Localization
items.summary: CLEW is a log-anchored backward tracing method for localizing root-cause code from issue descriptions and noisy runtime logs in industrial software systems.
items.why: Targets the practical problem of finding defect locations from incomplete logs, relevant to debugging production failures.

items.title: VAST: Compiling Grounded Vulnerability Scenarios into Verifiable, Multi-Step Environments for Evaluating LLM Red-Team Agents
items.summary: VAST is a declarative range compiler that generates verifiable, multi-step vulnerability environments for evaluating LLM red-team security agents.
items.why: Provides reproducible, diagnosable environments for testing security agents, which helps teams benchmark agent-based security tooling.

items.title: InvarOrd: Self-Supervised Ordinal Knowledge Distillation with Rank-Invariant Alignment for Label-Efficient Cross-Species Hyperspectral Fish Freshness Assessment
items.summary: InvarOrd is a self-supervised ordinal distillation method that adapts hyperspectral fish freshness models to new species using 30 labelled cubes.
items.why: Shows label-efficient cross-domain transfer for ordinal classification, though the application is niche for most engineering teams.

items.title: Do Probing and Steering Favor the Same Directions Within and Across Language Models?
items.summary: Researchers study whether directions that best probe a concept in LLM hidden states also work best for steering, testing a family of directions across three instruction-tuned models.
items.why: Shows probe directions may not be the best steering directions, which affects interpretability-based control methods.

items.title: Agent Authenticator: Passkey-Grade, Hardware-Bound Authentication for AI Agents
items.summary: Researchers propose Agent Authenticator, a hardware-bound, passkey-style authentication scheme for AI coding agents that currently rely on bearer tokens readable by models and malware.
items.why: Agents hold tokens for pushing code and cloud access, so bearer-secret exposure is a real security gap for engineering teams.

items.title: Func-JEPA: Learning a Sobolev Space of Functions as Latent Vectors
items.summary: Researchers introduce Func-JEPA, an encoder pretrained on symbolic mathematical functions whose latent space mimics a Sobolev space, so differentiation becomes a latent operator.
items.why: It proposes a shared, reusable function representation for symbolic math, a departure from training a separate model per task.

items.title: Beyond Prompts: Runtime Contracts for Coding Agents
items.summary: A study tests whether executable contracts enforced during a coding agent's work reduce rule violations better than writing the same rules in the prompt or checking after generation.
items.why: It suggests enforcing engineering rules in code, not prompts, may give teams verifiable compliance from coding agents.

items.title: Lesion-Aware Explainable AI for Diabetic Retinopathy Grading from Fundus Images
items.summary: Researchers propose CCEM, a consensus-calibrated explanation method for diabetic retinopathy grading that fuses several attribution methods using annotation-free reliability cues.

items.title: Inquest: Log-Guided Root-Cause Code Localization with a Staged Agent
items.summary: Researchers present Inquest, a staged agent that localizes root-cause code from production logs, with a benchmark of 38,001 resolved issues across 27 open-source projects.
items.why: Logs often point to where failures surface rather than their cause, so better localization could speed production debugging.

items.title: SemMask: Semantic-Prioritized Progressive Masking for Diffusion Language Models
items.summary: SemMask is a fine-tuning method for diffusion language models that uses semantic-prioritized progressive masking to decode high-information tokens early and reduce function-word-first bias.
items.why: It targets a known weakness of diffusion language models in code generation and writing tasks that need global planning.

items.title: Read, Then Shade? How Visual Evidence Changes Incentive-Driven Misreporting in Vision-Language Advisors
items.summary: A study examines whether a stated incentive changes what vision-language models report about a scene, and whether reading values from pixels rather than text alters that misreporting.
items.why: It raises reliability concerns when VLMs report to a receiver whose objectives may differ from the model's.

items.title: Learning from Mutants: Teaching Small Language Models to Synthesise Loop Invariants
items.summary: Researchers propose a failure-driven data curation method, inspired by mutation testing, to fine-tune small language models to synthesize loop invariants for program verification.
items.why: Small local models could automate loop invariant synthesis without relying on third-party frontier model APIs.

items.title: Spectral Steering: Local Inverse Geometry for Frozen Diffusion Generators
items.summary: Spectral Steering is a method for frozen diffusion generators that combines a cosine-gain predictor with damped inverse correction to realize structured output edits.

items.title: Risk-Averse Decision-Focused Learning: Minimizing CVaR of Regret
items.summary: Researchers propose risk-averse decision-focused learning that minimizes CVaR of regret, rather than expected regret, for combinatorial optimization under uncertainty.
items.why: High-stakes decisions under uncertain predictions may need tail-risk objectives instead of risk-neutral expected regret.

items.title: PBit1: One Programmable P-Bit per Parameter - A Finite-Control Representation of Pretrained Networks
items.summary: PBit1 proposes representing each pretrained network parameter with one programmable p-bit controlled by a 12-bit command, reconstructing weights for inference while preserving task quality.

items.title: Synthetic Neurosymbolic Task Generation with Controlled Constraint Complexity
items.summary: NeSySy is a synthetic generator for neurosymbolic learning tasks that produces logical constraints and consistent datasets with controllable constraint structure and tightness.
items.why: Configurable benchmarks with solver-verified constraints could help teams evaluate neurosymbolic methods more systematically.

items.title: Well-Log Reconstruction with Pre-trained Geological Knowledge: A Knowledge-Conditioned Large-Language-Model Generative Agent
items.summary: GeoLog-Agent is a knowledge-conditioned generative agent that uses pre-trained LLMs as geological priors to reconstruct missing well-log intervals.

items.title: Robust Well-Log Reconstruction Across Point Gaps and Whole Wells via Boundary-Gated Soft-Thresholding Kalman Fusion
items.summary: Researchers propose ST-KF, a boundary-gated soft-thresholding Kalman fusion method for reconstructing missing wireline logs, evaluated on two public benchmarks covering 263 wells.

items.title: Where slide-level foundation-model classifiers fail on atypical breast lesions
items.summary: A study finds slide-level classifiers built on pathology foundation models perform worst on atypical breast lesions, partly because slides are labelled with their most severe lesion.
items.why: Label noise from slide-level severity labeling can silently limit foundation-model performance in clinical deployments.

items.title: ROUNDS: Source-Framed Diagnostic Revision after Multi-Turn Clinical Evidence
items.summary: Researchers introduce ROUNDS, a framework testing whether LLMs keep reliable diagnoses across multi-turn clinical conversations, including unprompted options and others' opinions.
items.why: Benchmark scores may not reflect diagnostic reliability in real multi-turn clinical dialogue, so teams deploying medical assistants need conversation-level evaluation.

items.title: SG-LegalClarify: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Legal Reasoning and Ambiguity Recognition in Singapore Law
items.summary: Researchers release SG-LegalClarify, a large benchmark testing LLMs on Singapore legal reasoning and recognizing underspecified lay legal queries.
items.why: It shows LLMs may miss jurisdiction-specific doctrine and ambiguity, a risk for legal-domain products outside common-law generic knowledge.

items.title: LoopFill: Pipelined Multi-Token Speculative Decoding for Looped Transformers
items.summary: LoopFill is a training-free speculative decoding algorithm for looped LLMs that aims to reduce the sequential-pass latency of autoregressive generation.
items.why: Lower decoding latency for looped transformers could make parameter-efficient models cheaper to serve without retraining.

items.title: BadGCL: Towards Persistent Backdoor Attack on Graph Continual Learning Systems
items.summary: BadGCL shows that knowledge-preservation mechanisms in graph continual learning can keep early-injected backdoors alive across later task updates.
items.why: Teams updating graph models incrementally may retain poisoned behavior longer than expected, so update pipelines need security review.

items.title: Architecting the Corporate AI Infrastructure: The Evolving Roles of AI Governance Committees and Chief Ethics Officers
items.summary: A paper proposes a structured corporate AI governance infrastructure, addressing the gap that fewer than half of organizations citing AI governance have a formal framework.
items.why: It offers a concrete organizational model for AI governance committees and ethics officers, relevant to leaders building oversight processes.

items.title: MathaMAGICal: Validating Trajectory Data Attribution During Capability Acquisition
items.summary: Researchers evaluate MAGIC trajectory data attribution on GPT-2-style models, finding attribution scores correlate near chance with retraining results at 86M parameters.
items.why: Influence-based attribution may not reliably predict the effect of removing training data, so teams should validate it by retraining before relying on it.

items.title: Data Attribution Should Steer Pretraining
items.summary: The paper argues training-data attribution should be used to steer pretraining by identifying reusable data properties rather than one-off document rankings.
items.why: Reusable curation criteria could make pretraining data selection more transferable across runs, which matters for teams managing training budgets.

items.title: Where Should LLM Agents Adapt at Test Time? In Context, in Weights, or Both
items.summary: A study compares whether LLM agents should adapt at test time through in-context experience, weight updates, or both, across repeated environments.
items.why: Choosing between context-based memory and weight updates affects agent architecture and cost for repeated-task deployments.

items.title: Cache or Denoise Less? Residual Reuse in a Flow-Matching World Action Model
items.summary: Researchers compare cross-cycle caching against taking fewer denoising steps in Fast-WAM, a 6B-parameter flow-matching robot world action model.
items.why: Two uncached steps matched the success of ten on LIBERO-Goal, suggesting simpler step reduction can rival caching for robot policy latency.

items.title: Joint Learning of Factual and Counterfactual Worlds for Causal Prior-data Fitted Networks
items.summary: Researchers propose joint learning of factual and counterfactual worlds in causal prior-data fitted networks, pretrained on synthetic data for treatment effect estimation.

items.title: An Interpretable Acoustic Coordinate System for Japanese Consonant Morae in Dysarthric Speech
items.summary: Researchers propose an interpretable acoustic coordinate system giving distance-based visual feedback on Japanese consonant morae for dysarthric speech rehabilitation.

items.title: Exploration of Reinforcement Learning in Generative Recommendation Models
items.summary: A study revisits GRPO and ratio-based objectives for reinforcement learning in generative recommendation models, addressing unstable optimization and degraded quality.
items.why: Applying RL end-to-end to generative recommenders is unstable with naive GRPO, so practitioners need stabilizing objectives before adopting it.

items.title: How Far Is Too Far? Object Recognition Declines Monotonically with Semantic Distance
items.summary: ImageNet-OOC1k benchmark shows object recognition accuracy declines monotonically as semantic distance between object and background grows, across 35 vision models.
items.why: Vision models degrade predictably with object-background semantic mismatch, a robustness consideration for deployed perception systems.

items.title: StaleBench: Isolating Stale Retrieval in Agent Memory, and Pricing the Fix
items.summary: StaleBench isolates stale retrieval in agent memory using 892 updating facts and finds retrieval metrics can rank memory policies backwards.
items.why: Agents storing evolving facts may retrieve outdated versions, and standard retrieval metrics can misleadingly rank memory designs.

items.title: Learning Autoregressive Neural Operators on Solver-Defined Physical Constraint Manifolds
items.summary: PCM-NO is a projected-residual autoregressive neural operator that keeps predicted incompressible flow states within solver-defined physical constraints.
items.why: Enforcing solver constraints during autoregressive rollouts could make learned PDE surrogates more reliable for engineering simulation.

items.title: Eliciting Research Taste in LLMs through Future Research Direction Choice
items.summary: Researchers propose evaluating LLM research taste by having models choose which future research direction to pursue, given a research goal and current results.
items.why: It offers a way to measure LLM judgment in open-ended research, where no verifiable objective exists before a direction is chosen.

items.title: Reasoning in the loop: antibody lead optimization by probing mechanism and measurement
items.summary: Researchers examine lab-in-the-loop antibody lead optimization, arguing that metrics computed from instrument signals can be poor proxies that better models or more data cannot fix.
items.why: Teams building closed-loop ML systems should validate that optimization metrics actually reflect the properties they need, since proxy failures are not solved by more data.

items.title: GraphPass: A Study of Graph Neural Networks for Compiler Pass Selection
items.summary: Researchers study GraphPass, a graph neural network that reads a program's control-flow graph to select among five compiler pass sequences in one forward pass.
items.why: It suggests learned models could replace fixed -O2/-O3 pipelines and hand-written heuristics, though results are on a synthetic benchmark only.

items.title: The Flip Test: Video World Models Fail to Learn the World State
items.summary: Researchers introduce FlipTest, a hierarchy of counterfactual tests showing that video world models often fail to track the underlying state of a scene.
items.why: Teams relying on video world models for prediction or planning should not assume they track physical state, since these tests show frequent failures.

items.title: EfficientSkill: Learning Skills for Token-Efficient Multi-Turn Agents
items.summary: Researchers present EfficientSkill, a framework that prunes and compresses agent skill instructions to reduce token use and turns in multi-turn LLM agents.
items.why: Reducing prompt bloat and agent loop length can cut inference cost and error rates for teams running multi-turn agents.

items.title: Bridging the Terminology Gap: A Data-Centric Alignment Framework for Multilingual Translation in Cross-Border Corporation
items.summary: Researchers propose BTG, a data-centric framework that mines cross-lingual terminology and synthesizes terminology-rich parallel corpora to improve enterprise translation.
items.why: Enterprises with domain jargon across languages may benefit from terminology-focused data synthesis, though the text gives no benchmark results.

items.title: Local Order Matters: A Lightweight CPU-Trainable CNN for Website Fingerprinting on Defended Tor Traffic
items.summary: Researchers show a compact 1-D CNN trained on CPU can perform website fingerprinting against Tor traffic defended by the FRONT padding scheme.
items.why: It shows defended Tor traffic remains vulnerable to learned attacks, relevant to teams assessing anonymity and traffic-analysis risk.

items.title: HalluProbe: Exploiting VLM Hallucinations for Backdoor Detection
items.summary: Researchers propose HalluProbe, which uses vision-language model hallucinations to expose backdoor behavior induced by data poisoning.
items.why: Security teams deploying VLMs get a possible detection signal for poisoned backdoors, though the text gives no detection performance figures.

items.title: Let Execution Do the Teaching
items.summary: Researchers describe improving the GLM-4.7-Flash coding model using supervised fine-tuning, C++ repair curricula, and reinforcement learning with execution-based rewards.
items.why: Using compiler errors and test results as structured rewards offers a practical recipe for improving code models without relying only on human labels.

items.title: Large Language Model-based Optimization for Wireless Communication: A Survey
items.summary: A survey reviews how large language models are being applied to real-time optimization and resource allocation in wireless communication systems.
items.why: Engineers in telecom may find it useful as an overview of where LLMs can complement traditional optimization, though it reports no new results.

items.title: Recovery Gone Too Far: Understanding and Repairing Risky Fallback in LLM Agents
items.summary: Researchers study how LLM agents fall back to substitute tools after ordinary errors, showing the same fallback can be safe in one environment and risky in another.
items.why: Agents with tool fallback can cross action boundaries, such as forced pushes that overwrite others' work, so teams need guardrails tied to context.

items.title: AgenticJevNav: Agentic Object Search and Navigation via Event-Driven Verification
items.summary: Researchers present AgenticJevNav, an agentic navigation system that triggers event-driven verification after failed actions or repeated low-progress segments.
items.why: It illustrates bounded action sets and verification triggers for embodied agents, a pattern relevant to teams building reliable autonomous navigation.

items.title: The Vocabulary Tax: Safely Trimming Unused Tokens from LLMs for On-Device Use
items.summary: Researchers quantify unused vocabulary rows in 1,244 open models on Hugging Face and propose safely trimming them to reduce on-device model size.
items.why: Teams shipping models on-device could cut download size substantially by removing vocabulary rows their deployment never uses.

items.title: Learning When to Continue and When to Stop: Termination-Aware OPSD
items.summary: Researchers identify a termination mismatch in on-policy self-distillation, where students stop reasoning too early or over-generate, and propose a termination-aware fix.
items.why: Reasoning models that stop prematurely or repeat endlessly waste compute or give wrong answers, so stopping behavior is a practical training concern.

items.title: Equal Dose, Different Coverage:Tracing Rate and Duration in Image Editing
items.summary: Researchers find that in distilled FLUX with Chinese prompts, errors in scientific image editing stem from representations of rate and duration, not just the endpoint.
items.why: It highlights that correct final outputs can hide wrong internal dynamics, relevant to teams debugging or steering image-editing models.

items.title: Value and Policy Calibration from Execution Feedback for Socially Compatible Driving
items.summary: Researchers propose a world-model reinforcement learning framework that calibrates value and policy from executed interactions so autonomous vehicles balance progress with burden on human drivers at intersections.
items.why: Shows how learning from real execution feedback, not just imagined rollouts, may help AV planners reduce disruption to surrounding human drivers.

items.title: Federated Dataset Simulation: Inducing Label-Free Heterogeneity Across Tasks
items.summary: Researchers introduce a method to simulate federated datasets with label-free heterogeneity, aiming to replace label-skew partitioning that does not apply to non-classification tasks.
items.why: Gives FL engineers a more realistic way to evaluate federated systems beyond Dirichlet label-skew splits, including for non-classification tasks.

items.title: CreaTrace: Video Creative Plagiarism Detection and Evidence Tracing
items.summary: Researchers define Video Creative Plagiarism Detection, a task for finding reused creative ideas across videos that differ visually, and propose an iterative evidence-tracing framework.
items.why: Highlights that visual copy detection misses idea-level copying, relevant to teams building video copyright or content-moderation tooling.

items.title: Morphology-Decoupled Segmentation for Multiple Tunnel Defects Under Complex Environments
items.summary: Researchers propose Morphology-Decoupled Segmentation, which routes features and decoding by defect shape to segment cracks and other tunnel-lining defects in complex environments.

items.title: What Matters for Cross-Modal Alignment
items.summary: Researchers test zero-pair alignment of frozen encoders across five datasets and four modalities, finding it succeeds only on COCO natural images and fails on audio, radiographs, and CT.
items.why: Suggests cross-modal alignment without paired data does not generalize beyond natural images, a caution for teams assuming it transfers to medical or audio domains.

items.title: The novelty exposed: ablation, reproducibility and transparency in 40 technical reports of open-weight large language models (LLMs)
items.summary: A study of 40 sampled open-weight LLM technical reports examines whether claimed architectural novelties are supported by ablation studies and what reproducibility details are disclosed.
items.why: Helps engineers judge how much weight to give novelty claims in open-weight model reports, given how many new architectures appear each year.

items.title: ReactBench-AD: Do Driving VLAs and World-Action Models React to Imminent Hazards in Their Path?
items.summary: Researchers introduce ReactBench-AD, a benchmark testing whether driving VLA and world-action models react to imminent hazards appearing in the ego vehicle's path.
items.why: Targets long-tail safety behavior that nominal driving benchmarks miss, useful for teams evaluating autonomous driving models before deployment.

items.title: D'BEAST: Logged Bad Experiences as Explanation for Autonomous Driving Agents
items.summary: Researchers present D'BEAST, which replays a tabular RL training log under three conditions to test whether agent decisions can be explained by logged bad experiences.
items.why: Offers a replay-based method for tracing RL agent decisions to safety-relevant training events, relevant to explainability work in autonomous driving.

items.title: Improving fine-grained expressivity of graph neural networks
items.summary: A thesis investigates the expressive power of graph neural networks and symmetry-aware architectures, introducing EGenNet and characterizations of equivariant linear layers.
